order.title: Activation order
order.openTip: Activation order: which mod is applied first, and so which one wins a file two mods share
order.lede: Mods are applied from top to bottom. When two active mods ship the same file, the one lower in the list is applied later and its version is the one in the game.
order.empty: No active mod in this profile yet. Enable some mods and their order shows here.
order.noConflict: Shares no file with another active mod
order.dragHint: Drag a row, or select it and press Alt+↑/↓ (Alt+Home/End for top/bottom).
order.reapplyTip: Copy the winner of every shared file into the game again: the repair when the game folder and this order may disagree.
order.pendingNone: Order changed, no file changes hands
order.applyFailed: The order is saved, but the game folder could not be fully updated: {e}. Re-apply finishes the job.
order.discard: Unapplied changes. Close again to discard them
order.loadFailed: Could not read the activation order: {e}
order.lib.inactive: Enable this mod to place it in the order.
order.share.tip: Copy this order as a code, a link or a list, for another PC
order.share.title: Share the order
order.share.lede: {n} active mod(s), named by what another PC can recognize, never by local paths.
order.share.note: Importing it only reorders the mods active there. Nothing is enabled or disabled.
order.share.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text below instead.
order.import.tip: Paste a shared order and see where each mod lands
order.import.title: Import an order
order.import.paste: Paste a code, a bmm:// link, a JSON file or a list of names
order.import.placeholder: BMMORDER1.… or one mod name per line
order.import.inactiveHint: Enable them first to have them placed.
order.import.drafted: Imported as a draft. Check it, then Apply order.
order.errEmpty: No order found in this text.
order.errParse: This is not an order BMM can read.
order.errTooLarge: Too large to be an order.
order.errMode: Unknown placement. Use top, bottom or keep.
order.mode.label: Bulk enable
order.mode.tip: Where mods go in the order when several turn on at once: modpack, Enable all, mod list, task, script
orderList.openTip: Saved order lists: build an order from any mods, active or not, apply it to several profiles or turn its mods on in one step
orderList.title: Activation order lists
orderList.intro: A list is a saved order that can name any mod: active, installed but off, or not installed yet. Pick a list, create one, start from a profile's order, or import a shared one.
orderList.loadFailed: Could not read the order lists: {e}
orderList.fromProfileTip: Start a list from the active mods of the profile shown, in their current order
orderList.importedDraft: Imported as a new list. Check the matches, then Save.
orderList.name: Name
orderList.scopeHint: Tick the profiles this list is for. None ticked: a reusable list, for any profile.
orderList.emptyList: This list is empty. Add mods below: active or not.
orderList.q.idTip: Found by its BMM id on this PC
orderList.q.contentTip: Found by its content fingerprint: the same mod, whatever it is called
orderList.q.sourceTip: Found by the id it has in the repo it came from
orderList.q.name_versionTip: Found by its name, and the version agrees
orderList.q.name: Name only
orderList.q.nameTip: Found by its name only (case and spaces ignored). Worth a glance.
orderList.q.ambiguousTip: Several mods carry this name and nothing tells them apart: none is picked
orderList.q.missingTip: No mod of the library answers to this entry. It stays in the list.
orderList.saveFirst: Unsaved changes: Activate, Apply order and Share use the saved list.
orderList.shareCopied: Code copied. Paste it into Import on another PC.
orderList.applyTip: Give this order to the active mods of one or several profiles. Nothing is enabled or disabled.
orderList.applyLede: In each profile ticked, the active mods this list names take its order, in the slots they hold. Mods it does not name keep their place. Only the files that change hands are copied.
orderList.applyPartial: Order applied to {n} of {m} profile(s). See below.
orderList.activateTip: Turn on every installed mod of this list on the active profile, in the list's order
orderList.activateLede: The mods that are off are turned on (with their dependencies), then the list's mods are placed on top in its order: the last one wins a shared file. Only the files that change hands are copied.
orderList.exclusive: Only this list: also turn off the active mods it does not name (their dependencies stay)
orderList.background: Runs in the background: you can close this window, the activity bar at the top keeps its progress and its Stop.
orderList.activated: {n} mod(s) on, {d} turned off, {f} file(s) re-deployed, {m} not found.
orderList.activatedCancelled: Stopped: {n} mod(s) on, {d} turned off, {f} file(s) re-deployed.
orderList.failedSha: file hashes not computed yet (integrity check)
orderList.errTooMany: Too many saved lists. Delete some first.
orderList.errNotActive: A list is activated on the active profile only. Switch to that profile first.
orderList.viewState: Show the state of the mods in {p}
orderList.viewingTip: The chips of each row say where the mod stands in this profile. Click the eye on another profile to see it from there.
orderList.sum.activeTip: Already on in the profile shown
orderList.sum.inactiveTip: Installed but off: Activate turns them on
orderList.sum.missingTip: Not found in the library: they stay in the list and are skipped
orderList.st.activeTip: On in {p}, at position {n} of its order
orderList.st.inactiveTip: Installed in {p} but off: Activate turns it on
orderList.st.outsideTip: Installed on this PC, but not part of {p}
orderList.pick.hint: Up/Down to browse, Enter to add, click to select several
orderList.pick.emptyLib: The library has no mod yet.
orderList.addFromProfileTip: Append the active mods of {p}, in their current order, skipping those already listed
orderList.notesTip: Notes for this list, written in B.MD (Markdown). Shown above the list.
orderList.notesPlaceholder: What this list is for, what to install first… B.MD is supported.
orderList.notesCountTip: Notes hold up to 20,000 characters. For a longer write-up, link to it.
orderList.saveFailed: Not saved. Check the name and the notes.
orderList.errNotesTooLong: The notes are longer than 20,000 characters. Shorten them to save.
orderList.errFile: This is not a list file BMM can read (.bmmorder).
orderList.importedTip: This list came from somebody else. Its notes are shown in safe mode: no HTML, nothing loaded from the internet (images, videos and embeds are left out), diagrams drawn in strict mode.
orderList.importPaste: Paste a code, a link or a list of mod names, or open a .bmmorder file
orderList.view.label: View
orderList.shareLede: The order and the notes travel together. On the other PC: Lists, then Import.
orderList.shareCodeLede: One line to paste in a chat or a forum post.
orderList.shareTooLong: Too long for a code: share the file instead. It carries the whole list, notes included.
orderList.shareFileLede: The whole list as a file, whatever its size.
orderList.shareFileLedeNotes: The whole list as a file, with its {n} characters of notes.
order.errVersion: Made by a newer BMM. Update BMM to read it.
order.sortTip: Sort the draft once; drag or Alt+arrows to fine-tune
order.resetTip: Back to the order that is in the game
order.applyTip: Save this order and copy only the files that change hands
plugins.actionArrangeModOrderDesc: What a modpack does after enabling its mods: top makes them win, bottom keeps the others winning, keep moves nothing.
plugins.actionImportModOrderDesc: A BMMORDER1 code, a bmm://order link or a list of names. Only reorders active mods; enables nothing.
plugins.dl.order.a: Opens the activation order with the shared order in the import preview. Nothing moves until you take it and press Apply order.
plugins.dl.order.p.d: The order code (BMMORDER1.…), from Share in the order view.
plugins.dl.modpack_enable.p.order: Where its mods go in the order: top, bottom or keep. Default: the pack's choice, then the setting.
plugins.epAbout.orderExport: The profile's order as a portable document: code, link, text and doc. Mods are named by fingerprint, repo id and name, never by local path.
plugins.epAbout.orderImport: Reads a code, a bmm://order link, the JSON or a list of names. The active mods it names take its order in their slots; nothing is enabled or disabled. dryRun answers the plan only.
plugins.ep.orderArrange: Place a block of active mods
plugins.epAbout.orderArrange: What a bulk enable ends with. top: the block wins. bottom: what was active keeps winning. keep: nothing moves. No mode = the setting.
plugins.epAbout.orderModeGet: Where a bulk enable places its mods when it does not say: top, bottom or keep.
plugins.epAbout.orderModeSet: Saves the default placement of a bulk enable. It moves nothing by itself.
plugins.epF.orderMode: top, bottom or keep. Empty: the pack's own choice, then the setting.
plugins.epF.orderProfile: Which profile. Default: the active one.
plugins.epF.orderIds: Active mod ids, first applied first.
sched.place.label: Activation order
modpack.orderHint: Order in which the pack's mods are applied, on top of the profile's order. The last one wins a shared file.
tut.basics.conflicts.order1.title: Choose who wins
tut.basics.conflicts.order1.text: Both example mods ship Mods/shared/config.ini. The one applied last wins, set in the profile's Activation order. Open it from the example profile's card, move Example Texture Pack to the bottom (drag it, or select it and press Alt+↓), see its row show Overrides 1 file, then click Apply order.
tut.basics.conflicts.order1.action: Reorder the two example mods and click Apply order
tut.basics.conflicts.order2.title: Only what changed hands moves
tut.basics.conflicts.order2.text: BMM re-copied only config.ini, the file whose winner changed. Disabling follows the same order: turn the winner off and the next mod's copy comes back, or the game's original. Applied modpacks put their mods on top, in the pack's order.
tut.basics.conflicts.s1b.text: Click a conflict badge to open the Conflict Resolver. It lists each clashing file and which mod currently wins (the higher activation order). Change the order or pick a winner per file to decide which config.ini ends up in the game.
tut.advanced.repo.f.tabsync: Sync tab: join a repo and download its mods.
tut.advanced.repo.f.tabhost: Host tab: build a repo from your library and serve it.
tut.advanced.repo.s4.title: You’re a host now
tut.advanced.repo.s4.text: That's the whole loop: Host generates + serves, teammates Sync from the URL. Update a mod, regenerate, and everyone re-syncs only what changed (delta). Great for a group all running the exact same modded setup.
tut.basics.map.s4.action: Select a mod from the dropdown
tut.basics.moddetails.s2.action: Click a mod to open its details
tut.basics.moddetails.f.edit: Save: keep your name / version / author edits (pencil to edit).
tut.basics.moddetails.s4.title: Integrity and content ID
tut.basics.moddetails.s4.text: Two trust tools. Verify re-hashes every tracked file and tells you if anything changed. The content ID is the whole mod's fingerprint: compare it to check two installs are the same mod.
tut.basics.moddetails.f.verify: Verify: re-check this mod's files against their hashes.

faq.cust.q1: How do I customize the navigation bar?
faq.cust.a1: Open Settings → the toolbar at the top of the cards → "Customize navigation". You can drag to reorder tabs, hide or rename them, group them into sections, and add your own buttons (open an internal tab, a dialog, an external URL, or a custom page). Pick any icon, and share your layout via a bmm:// link.
faq.cust.a2: Custom pages are tiny HTML/CSS/JS/WASM apps you add to the navbar. Create one from the "Custom pages" section of the Customize navigation editor. Each page renders inside BMM, in the content area, while the navbar stays available.
faq.cust.q3: Are custom pages safe? Can they access my mods or files?
faq.cust.a3: No. Every page runs in a strict sandbox (isolated iframe, opaque origin, locked-down Content-Security-Policy). It cannot reach BMM, your mods, your files, the system, the network or other pages. Its only link is the bmm API, and every capability is denied until you grant it for that page.
faq.cust.q4: Can a custom page access the internet or store data?
faq.cust.a4: Only if you allow it. In the Custom pages list, each page has toggles: storage (a private 2 MB key/value store, namespaced to that page), notify (BMM toasts), internet (GET only, and only to the exact origins you allow-list), and app info (a few non-sensitive read-only values). Everything is off until you turn it on. Full API docs are in the "Custom Pages API" tab.
faq.cust.q5: An external URL button shows a blank page. Why?
faq.cust.a5: Some sites (YouTube, Google…) forbid being embedded in a frame (their server sends X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors). That is the sites choice and cannot be bypassed. Use the "Open in browser" button in the pages top bar, or pick a site that allows embedding.

docs.pagesApi.intro: Custom pages are small HTML/CSS/JS/WASM apps you add to the navbar (Settings → Customize navigation → Custom pages). Each page runs in a fully isolated sandbox. A page cannot reach BMM, your mods, files, the system, the network, or any other page. Its only link to BMM is the global bmm object, and every method requires a permission you grant per-page (everything is denied by default).
docs.pagesApi.capStorage: bmm.storage.* — a private key/value store (2 MB), namespaced to this page only.
docs.pagesApi.capNet: bmm.fetch() — GET, but only to the origins you explicitly allow-list for the page. Once granted, a plain fetch() to those origins works too.
docs.pagesApi.capRead: bmm.read() — a few non-sensitive values (app name/version/platform/lang, current theme). Never your data, files, or settings.
docs.pagesApi.writeP: Inline event handlers (onclick="…") and inline <script> are blocked by the page CSP. Put your code in the JS box and use addEventListener. The bmm object is available globally. WASM works: WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(module.wasm)) can load a .wasm that ships inside the page (own-bundle fetch is allowed; the internet is not, unless granted).
docs.pagesApi.secNote: Security: a denied call rejects with permission_denied; an internet call to a non-allow-listed origin rejects with origin_not_allowed. There is no way for a page to read BMM internals, run system code, or touch another page's data.
docs.pagesApi.start1: Open Settings → Customize navigation → Custom pages and click Create page.
docs.pagesApi.start2: Fill the HTML, CSS and JS boxes. Your JS goes into app.js; inline onclick/<script> are blocked, so wire events with addEventListener.
docs.pagesApi.start3: Grant the permissions the page needs (use a preset: Strict / Mid / Low), and for internet add the allowed origins.
docs.pagesApi.start4: Add a navbar button of type Custom page pointing at it. Re-open the page (switch tab and back) after changing permissions so the new rules apply.
docs.pagesApi.start5: Need a binary asset (e.g. a .wasm)? Use Import file on the page, then load it with a relative URL (fetch('module.wasm')).
docs.pagesApi.cStorageClear: Removes everything stored by this page.
docs.pagesApi.cFetch: GET an allow-listed URL → { status, body } (body is text). Works around CORS (done server-side).
docs.pagesApi.cRead: A safe read-only value (see scopes below), or null.
docs.pagesApi.callsNote: Every call returns a Promise. If the permission isn’t granted it rejects with permission_denied (and a toast names the missing permission).
docs.pagesApi.cClipWrite: Copies text to the system clipboard. Resolves true.
docs.pagesApi.cSystem: Safe read-only system facts (see shape below). No filesystem, processes, or shell.
docs.pagesApi.capClipboard: bmm.clipboard.* — read/write the system clipboard (on a user action).
docs.pagesApi.capSystem: bmm.system.info() — safe, read-only hardware/OS facts (OS, arch, CPU count, RAM, uptime). Never the filesystem, processes, shell, or your identity.

tut.quick.meta.title: The five-minute tour
tut.quick.meta.desc: What BMM is, one stop per big idea. No actions, no modals - just where everything lives. The longer tutorials teach you to USE each piece; this one makes sure you know it exists.
tut.quick.tour.title: The tour
tut.quick.tour.s1.title: The Library is home
tut.quick.tour.s1.text: Every mod BMM knows about lives here - with its version, author, tags and state. A green toggle means the mod's files are applied to the game right now; grey means they are safely stored, ready to apply. Nothing you do in this list touches the game until you flip a toggle.
tut.quick.tour.s2.title: Mods come in here
tut.quick.tour.s2.text: Add a mod imports from a folder or an archive. BMM copies the files into its own storage and fingerprints every one of them - which is what later lets it verify nothing got corrupted, detect conflicts, and undo cleanly.
tut.quick.tour.s3.title: Verify is your safety net
tut.quick.tour.s3.text: This re-hashes every stored file and compares it against the fingerprint taken at import. A mod that passes is byte-for-byte what you imported; one that fails has been changed, corrupted, or half-deleted - and BMM tells you which files.
tut.quick.tour.s4.title: Profiles keep games apart
tut.quick.tour.s4.text: A profile is one game (or one playthrough): its own mod list, its own game folder, its own backups. Switching profiles switches everything at once, so two games - or two setups of the same game - can never contaminate each other.
tut.quick.tour.s5.title: Modpacks are recipes
tut.quick.tour.s5.text: A modpack is a named set of mods you apply in one click - 'my multiplayer set', 'vanilla plus'. It records which mods and in what order, so a working combination is something you can come back to, share, or ship in a repo.
tut.quick.tour.s6.title: The Mapper untangles folders
tut.quick.tour.s6.text: Some mods ship with the wrong folder layout for your game. The Mapper shows the mod's structure next to the game's, and lets you re-map where each part lands - without editing the mod itself. The original files stay untouched.
tut.quick.connect.title: Connecting & beyond
tut.quick.connect.s1.title: Server repos: mods from a URL
tut.quick.connect.s1.text: Paste a repository URL here and BMM can pull a whole curated mod set - with integrity hashes, so every download is verified. If the server has no repo.json at all, BMM reads its folder index instead and installs the mods marked as unverified, telling you exactly what that means.
tut.quick.connect.s2.title: Fetch first, decide after
tut.quick.connect.s2.text: Fetch downloads nothing but the manifest: you see the repo's name, author, signature status and every profile it offers before a single mod file moves. Protected repo? There is a password row right under the URL field.
tut.quick.connect.s3.title: Settings - and the look
tut.quick.connect.s3.text: Language, backups, Tasky the mascot, performance, themes - all here. Tip: press Ctrl+K anywhere and type what you want ('style', 'export', 'verify'...) - the command palette reaches almost everything faster than any menu.
tut.quick.connect.s4.title: When in doubt: Help & Other
tut.quick.connect.s4.text: The full documentation lives in the app: how syncing verifies files, what the Mapper actually does, and interactive diagrams you can click through. That's the tour! The other tutorials in the hub go deeper on each stop, whenever you want them.

sched.actd.list.set: Replaces the whole list. Accepts a JSON array or a plain a, b, c line. Read it back with {list.<name>.length}, or walk it with FOR EACH.
sched.actd.list.push: Adds one item to the end. Unlike “set it”, running twice appends twice.
sched.actd.list.clear: Empties the list without deleting its name, so a later push starts from nothing.
sched.actd.map.set: Stores one value under one key. A list answers “which ones”; a map answers “what goes with what”.
sched.actd.map.get: Reads one key into a variable. A missing key gives an empty value; {map.hit} tells if it existed.
sched.actd.map.clear: Empties the map without deleting its name.

docs.diagram.deeplinks.title: Deep links (bmm://)
docs.diagram.app-catalog.title: App Catalog
docs.diagram.app-catalog.summary: Where the app list comes from, how each entry gets its badge, and the checks an install goes through before anything runs.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.OFFICIAL.desc: The catalog.json named by apps_catalog in links.json. It is the only source of the Official badge, and the only one allowed to name partner catalogues.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.PARTNER.desc: The URLs listed in the official catalogue's partner_catalogs. Their entries get the Partner badge; a partner cannot name further partners.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.COMMUNITY.des: Catalogue URLs you add in the Sources tab (a BetterCommunity catalog.json feed included), plus the community_imports any catalogue chains to. No badge, whatever the file says. At most 30 sources load, and a source switched off is kept but not fetched.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.BUNDLE.desc: A catalogue that carries its apps in one file on this disk (a zip with catalog.json and the payloads). It is opened locally and its entries are merged into the list, with nothing to host.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.FETCH.desc: Fetches each source with a 15-second timeout, skipping URLs already visited. A key proof is attached when this BMM has one; the X-Creator-ID header goes only to BetterCommunity hosts, so private catalogues there can gate by account. A failing source is logged; only all of them failing shows an error.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.TRUST.desc: Official and Partner are set from where an entry was fetched, never from what the JSON claims. A claim higher than the source's tier is kept and shown as "claims official" next to the source. Duplicates by id keep the highest tier; tags are capped at 3.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.BROWSE.desc: Search and filter by category and price, favourites in collections, and a History tab. Each card says whether the catalogue publishes a checksum and whether the download is plain http.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.INSTALL_APP.d: https is accepted; plain http only after you accept the warning; any other scheme is refused. The app id must be one plain folder name. The payload streams to a .part file while it is hashed, and stops at 4 GiB.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.CHECKSUM.desc: Checked before the file is renamed or run. A mismatch, or no checksum in the catalogue, opens a warning that shows the hashes; only an explicit "install anyway" continues. A bmm:// install link gets no such choice: it needs a matching sha256.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.DROPPED.desc: Declined or failed: the .part file is removed, so an unverified payload is never left on disk and never executed.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.SETUP.desc: An .msi or a setup is run, then its program is found from the Windows uninstall registry or the new folders it created. A zip is extracted with the zip-slip guard and size caps, and may itself hold an installer. A plain .exe is kept as a portable app.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.STATE.desc: Installed apps with their folder and main executable, favourites, community sources, usage time and the last 200 history entries.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.LAUNCH.desc: Installed apps start from their card with the registered executable, which you can change. Uninstall runs the app's own uninstaller when it has one, or removes the folder.
docs.diagram.app-catalog.n.CREATE.desc: Builds your own catalogue: entries filled by probing a URL or a local file (size and SHA-256), saved as catalog.json, or published as one .bmmbundle that packs the payloads.
docs.diagram.app-update.title: BMM self-update
docs.diagram.app-update.summary: How BMM finds a newer release of itself, and the three ways it installs one without ever running an unchecked file.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.START.desc: Runs 3 seconds after launch when automatic updates are on (the default), from the Check for updates buttons, and from the scheduler's update action. A line DisableUpdate=true in app.cfg switches every button and the startup check off.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.LINKS.desc: Gives the two feed addresses: autoupdate_api (GitHub releases) and autoupdate_api_fallback (BetterCommunity, /api/updates/bmm). links.json itself is read from BetterCommunity first, then its GitHub copy, then the bundled file, then built-in defaults.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.FEED.desc: GitHub's releases API, or BetterCommunity, which serves the same shape. With pre-releases off BMM asks for the latest release; with them on, for the newest of the list.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.FETCH.desc: Asks the primary feed (10 second timeout). A network error or a rate limit (403 or 429) moves on to the fallback; a 404 does not, it means there is no release. It picks the installer asset and the update-manifest.json asset, and flags a major version bump.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.BI_CHECK.desc: When BMM was installed by BetterInstaller, uninstall.exe --check-update is asked too, and its answer (version and notes) replaces the feed's, since it is exactly what its update will apply. Otherwise the feed's answer stands.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.NEWER.desc: Compares the dotted numbers of both versions, a missing part counting as 0. It is the same rule the signed manifest check uses, so the dialog never offers an update the manifest would then refuse as not newer.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.UPTODATE.desc: The settings line shows the current version; a manual check also says so in a toast. No release yet or no network is shown quietly, not as an error.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.MODAL.desc: Shows both versions and the release notes. Quick Update is offered only when the release publishes a signed manifest and is not a major version; a major version installs by hand with the full installer, which migrates data and settings.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.QUICK.desc: Fetches update-manifest.json (https, at most 1 MB) and verifies it, then verifies it again in apply_incremental_update before writing. Each listed file is skipped when its SHA-256 already matches, otherwise downloaded, checked and moved into the install folder, with progress events per file.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.BI_UPDATE.desc: The Full installer button first tries uninstall.exe --update: BetterInstaller downloads and verifies its signed package, applies a delta when one is offered, rolls back on failure, and BMM exits so its files can be replaced.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.FULL.desc: For a copy BetterInstaller did not install. The installer URL must be one the verified manifest lists, the download is capped at 1 GB, its SHA-256 must match, and the file name comes from the manifest. It is saved in a fresh temp folder, launched, and BMM exits.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.VERIFY.desc: The manifest must carry an ed25519 signature from the publisher key compiled into BMM, name this app, be valid for at most 7 days and not expired, offer a strictly newer version, and list only https URLs, SHA-256 hashes and plain relative paths.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.STAY.desc: Any failed rule refuses the update before a file is written or run, with the reason in a toast and in the log. A release without a signed manifest cannot be installed from the app: the installer is downloaded from the release page by hand.
docs.diagram.app-update.n.RESTART.desc: After a Quick Update BMM reports how many files were applied, skipped or failed and asks for a restart. The installer paths close BMM themselves and the installer takes over.
docs.diagram.backup-system.title: Backups: game originals and BMM data
docs.diagram.backup-system.summary: The two things BMM backs up: the game files a mod replaces (_original/) and its own data (data.json.bak, .DATABMM archives).
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.ENABLE.desc: Before each mod file is copied into the game folder, BMM looks at the file it is about to overwrite.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.IS_ORIGINAL: A real game file, not saved yet?
Backed up only if the file exists, is not already in _original/, and was not put there by a mod of any profile sharing this game folder. Another mod's file is never mistaken for an original.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.ORIGINALS.d: The vanilla file is copied once, keeping its relative path, into the profile's backup folder (Backups/<profile id> in BMM's data folder when none was chosen). The copy runs under the governor's Backup rules for that disk. An existing copy is never overwritten.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.DISABLE.des: For each of its files, another active mod that provides it is copied back first. Only when no mod provides it any more does the original come back.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.RESTORED.de: The original is taken from this profile's _original/ or from the backup folder of another profile on the same game folder, copied back, then deleted from the backup to free the space. Empty folders left in _original/ are removed.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.SAVE.desc: data.json (profiles, mods, settings) is written crash-safe: the current file is copied to data.json.bak, the new one goes to a temporary file, is flushed to disk, then renamed over.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.DATA_BAK.de: The previous good version, rewritten at every save. If data.json is missing or unreadable at startup, BMM recovers from it.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.EXPORT_UI.d: Settings and the scheduler's backup action share one routine. Sections are ticked one by one: app data, themes, launch packs, automations, navigation and apps by default; replays, crash reports and diagnostics off. Identity keys are never included without a passphrase.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.BUNDLE.desc: Builds a zip with a manifest of what went in, sealed with the passphrase when one is given. A scheduled backup gets its file name from a template ({date}, {time}) and never silently overwrites yesterday's file unless asked to.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.DATABMM.des: One file holding the chosen sections, written where you chose. It holds BMM's data, not the game files or the mods themselves.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.RESTORE.des: The archive is opened (asking for the passphrase if it is sealed) and its sections listed; only the ticked ones are put back. An archive from someone else needs your explicit yes, and its scheduled tasks come back disabled.
docs.diagram.backup-system.n.BEFORE.desc: Before app data is replaced, the current data.json is copied under a timestamped name, so a restore can always be undone by hand. It is not the rolling .bak, which the next save would overwrite.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.title: BLAKE3 and SHA-256: which hash where
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.summary: Local mod hashes are BLAKE3, computed one file per thread on a capped pool; SHA-256 stays for legacy baselines, mod identity, repositories and updates.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.FILES.desc: Every file of a folder mod. An archived mod is read from its extracted view, so a zipped mod and its unzipped twin get the same hashes.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.POOL.desc: Files are hashed in parallel ACROSS files on the disk governor's Hash pool: half the cores, at most 4, under the Balanced preset (1 thread in Silent, cores minus one in Everything for BMM). Between files it checks its ticket, so a deploy, game mode or a cancel can make it step aside.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.HASH.desc: BLAKE3 over a memory-mapped file, sequentially on one thread: the multi-core tree mode is deliberately not used, so one huge file cannot take every core. The result is tagged b3:<hex>.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.MATCH.desc: file_matches_hash re-hashes a file with the algorithm the stored value names: b3: means BLAKE3, anything else is read as a legacy SHA-256. Old baselines and old modpacks keep verifying after the switch.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.SHA.desc: Plain SHA-256 (sha2 crate), read in 1 MB blocks for legacy baselines. It is also what the identity, repository and update code computes, on its own.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.BASELINE.d: The per-file file_hashes the SHA worker records and get_mod_integrity compares against.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.MODPACK.de: A modpack lists each file with its hash, stored in the field still named sha256 for compatibility but holding a b3: value. Checking a pack and finding a file by hash both go through file_matches_hash.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.HASHFILE.d: Hashes one file for the scheduler's verify steps and scripts: BLAKE3 by default (returned without the b3: tag) or SHA-256 on request, under a Hash ticket.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.CONTENT_ID: A mod's cross-machine identity: the id in its bmm.json, or else a SHA-256 of its sorted (path, size) pairs. No content is read, and it kept SHA-256 so the switch to BLAKE3 changed no mod's identity.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.REPO.desc: repo.json carries a SHA-256 per file, plus one per 4 MB chunk for large files. Sync compares local files with it, and a downloaded file that does not match is refused.
docs.diagram.blake3-hashing.n.UPDATE.des: The signed update manifest gives a SHA-256 for every file and installer. A Quick Update file or a downloaded installer that does not match is not applied.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.title: BMMScript
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.summary: How BMMScript text becomes the same step tree as the blocks, and the three places it comes from: the Code tab, a .bmmscript file and a code.run step.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.REF.desc: gen-bmms-reference.mjs extracts every action, condition, value and loop source from the scheduler's own lists, with parameter names from the runner. It writes the docs reference pages and the index the editor completes from; its --check mode fails the build when the two drift apart.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.CODE_TAB.d: The task editor's code mode: syntax highlighting, completion, an outline and hover help. Errors are checked while typing, but the line being typed is left alone until the caret moves away.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.FILE.desc: BMM registers itself as the program for .bmmscript. A file opened while BMM is closed is kept until the window exists, then compiled. One file can hold several tasks.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.CODE_RUN.d: A step whose body is BMMScript statements, compiled each time the step runs rather than stored compiled, so an edit can never leave an old version running. A syntax error fails the step with its line and column.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.LEX.desc: Lexes and parses a whole task (header with trigger, description, allow list) or bare statements. do name(key: value) becomes that action with those parameters, so every action is writable without the language listing them. The CLI and MCP server mount the same file.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.OK.desc: Any error stops the compile and returns one diagnostic with its line and column. Nothing half-compiled is ever kept or run.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.TREE.desc: The exact JSON the block editor produces: steps, conditions, trigger and permissions. Code cannot gain a capability the blocks do not have, because the blocks' runner is what runs it.
Prints a tree back as BMMScript every time the Code tab opens, so the text is never a stale copy of blocks edited since. Source to tree to source is kept stable by tests.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.LINEMAP.de: Which line each step starts on, for the debugger in code mode: the line lit while a run stands on a step, and the step a click in the gutter puts a breakpoint on.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.REVIEW.des: A file is never run on open: its steps are listed, scripts shown in full. A file that grants itself nothing runs in one click; one that asks for programs, scripts, links, deletion or other grants needs I have read what it does ticked first.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.SAVED.desc: Saved from the editor into schedules.json. A task added from a file arrives disabled, with every permission reset to off, to be granted one by one.
docs.diagram.bmmscript-flow.n.RUNNER.des: The same runner as any task: permissions, variables, loop caps and error handling. A file run once gets a temporary id, shows in the running panel and never registers a Windows task.
docs.diagram.cache-management.title: Mod caches: what BMM keeps and when it drops it
docs.diagram.cache-management.summary: The in-memory file index behind the Library and conflicts, the file lists saved in data.json, and the extracted copies of archived mods.
Listing the mods with their conflicts, enabling a mod and the conflict views all need to know which files each mod has. They ask for the index first.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.FRESH.de: A single marker says whether the index is up to date. There is no timer: it stays valid until something resets it.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.INDEX.de: For each mod, the set of its files; for each file, the mods that provide it. Conflicts are read from here instead of from the disk.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.INVALIDA: Resets the marker so the next request rebuilds. Called when mods are added, removed or remapped, when a profile's mods folder changes and when a profile is deleted.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.FLUSH.de: Switching to another view empties the front-end conflict cache and asks flush_mem_caches to free the file sets and the index, to give the memory back. Never while mods are being turned on or off.
For each mod, the folder's modification time is compared with the one stored at the last scan. Same time: the stored list is reused without walking the folder. A folder that cannot be reached (drive unplugged) keeps its old list.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.ARCHIVE_: An archived mod (.zip, .7z...) is listed from the archive's own index: nothing is extracted while the index is built.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.WALK.des: A changed folder mod is walked again and its new list stored.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.HASH_QUE: A changed mod that had hashes is queued for the throttled background hasher, one mod at a time, after every lock is released, so a big mod never freezes the window.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.CACHED_F: Each mod keeps its file list and the modification time it was taken at. That is what makes the next start cheap.
docs.diagram.cache-management.n.EXTRACTE: When an archived mod's files are actually needed (enable, hashing, a modpack), it is extracted once to a folder named after the archive's name, size and date, marked as complete. A changed archive gets a new folder; BMM does not delete the old ones.
docs.diagram.code-stack.title: BMM technology stack
docs.diagram.code-stack.summary: The layers BMM is built from: a TypeScript page in the OS webview, one invoke() bridge, a Rust core, and the API and CLI beside it.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.PAGE.desc: One HTML page holds every view. Its styles read the --bmm-* tokens of css/tokens.css, which is what themes override. A few small vendored scripts (GSAP for the intro, marked and DOMPurify for markdown) load with it.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.MODULES.desc: The app's code is TypeScript under frontend/src, compiled by tsc into plain ES modules in frontend/js: there is no bundler. ui/app.js is the one entry the page loads, and it imports the rest.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.LAZY.desc: Heavy libraries that only one screen needs (mermaid for diagrams, svg-pan-zoom, KaTeX) are fetched the first time that screen asks, then cached. A build gate fails if a blocking script in index.html passes 256 KB, or 512 KB in total.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.BRIDGE.desc: core/api.ts wraps the Tauri bridge: every call to the Rust core is invoke(command, args). A call made before the bridge is ready waits for it, and a failure is classified (error, cancel, network, validation) before it reaches a toast.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.BUILDER.desc: main.rs builds the app: the Tauri plugins (dialog, fs, shell, notification, process, cli, single instance), the bmmpage:// protocol for custom pages, and the list of every command the page may call. WebView2 features BMM does not use are switched off before the window exists, to save memory.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.COMMANDS.desc: One module per area under src-tauri/src/commands (mods, profiles, repos, themes, settings and more). Long disk work runs in a blocking task off the async runtime, so the window never waits for it.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.STATE.desc: The one in-memory state: profiles, mods and settings behind a single lock, plus caches that are never saved (conflict index, hash queues). It is written back atomically: a temporary file, flushed, then renamed over data.json.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.GOVERNOR.desc: Every heavy operation takes a ticket of its kind (deploy, hash, extract, download and so on). The governor sizes a thread pool per kind, rate-limits copies per disk, and pauses background work while a game runs.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.WORKER.desc: Applying and removing a mod's files runs in a second copy of the executable started with --mod-worker, which never opens a window. Cancelling kills that process, then an inverse pass undoes what it had written.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.API.desc: A warp server on 127.0.0.1 (port 51274 by default) that shares the app's live state with plugins, scripts and the MCP server. Every request needs a token, and only a 127.0.0.1 or localhost Host header is accepted.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.MCP.desc: A separate executable shipped beside the app: a command line and an MCP server (JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout) for AI clients. It reads data.json directly and goes through the local API for anything the running app has to do.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.DATA.desc: data.json (profiles, mods, settings) lives in the app data folder, next to themes and crash reports. A data folder left by the old bundle id is copied across on first start, before data.json is read.
docs.diagram.code-stack.n.NET.desc: Outside the app: repositories, catalogs and updates over HTTPS through one shared reqwest client (rustls), Discord Rich Presence, and the game folders on disk.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.title: Conflicts and activation order
docs.diagram.conflict-management.summary: How BMM finds mods that ship the same file, how it shows them, and how the activation order decides which copy is in the game.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.INDEX: An in-memory map from each relative path to the mods that ship it, built from the mods' file lists (archives listed from their own index). Conflicts are read here, never by walking the disk.
For each mod, counts the files it shares with every other mod. One batched call computes the whole library under a single lock pass. Only mods that can meet are reported: same profile, or another profile on the same game folder whose mods folder holds the other mod.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.KIND: Intra or Inter, active or potential
Intra: both mods are in this profile. Inter: the other one belongs to another profile on the same game folder. Active: both are enabled, so one copy really overwrites the other on disk. Potential: they would, once both are on.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.BADGE: Each card gets an Intra and/or Inter badge, red when active and amber when potential, kept between launches. Clicking one opens the global conflict list, filterable by profile, type and status.
Switching on a mod that has conflicts first shows which mods it overlaps, and for active ones their current position in the order. Activate anyway, or cancel. A checkbox can turn this warning off for good.
Lists the files two mods share (the first 2000, with the total) and says which mod's copy is on disk now. When both are on, a button makes the other one win.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.ACTIV: The profile's list of active mods IS the deployment order: first applied first, the last one wins every file it shares. There is no per-file choice and no priority number. Enabling a mod puts it at the end, on top.
Shows the active mods in order with who overrides whom, and before you apply a new order, how many files would change hands.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.SET.d: The new order must be exactly the same set of active mods, reordered; anything else is refused. It is saved for the profile and for twins that share its game and mods folders.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.REDEP: Re-copy the files that change hands

Only files whose winner changed are copied again, from the new winner (archived mods from their extracted cache), as one Deploy operation, one mod operation at a time. No backup: the file replaced belongs to another mod.
docs.diagram.conflict-management.n.REAPP: Re-copies the winner of every contested file, not just the moved ones. It is the repair after a reorder that stopped half-way, or after someone edited the game folder by hand.
The game folder now matches the order. A file no provider still has on disk is left as it was and counted, rather than deleted.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.title: Crash reports
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.summary: What writes a crash or session report, what goes into the zip, how secrets are removed, and where it shows up next.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.PANIC.des: A panic hook installed at start-up logs the panic message and writes a crash report straight away, from inside the failing process.
An uncaught error or unhandled promise rejection in the window builds a dump (recent logs, IPC calls, actions, app state) and sends it to trigger_manual_crash_report. The DevTools button does the same on demand.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.DIRTY.des: At start-up, a session_<pid>.log left by a process that is gone and that never wrote [SHUTDOWN] means BMM died without warning (killed, power cut). Its content becomes a crash report, then the log is deleted.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.CLEAN_EXI: Closing from the window marks the session clean, saves data.json and writes a session report with a data snapshot on a background thread; the window closes when it is done.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.LOG.desc: Every log line goes to a 500-line memory ring and is appended and flushed to Crashes/session_<pid>.log at once, so it survives a hard crash.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.REPLAY.de: The session is always recorded and flushed every 45 s (and on close) to last_crash_session.bmmreplay. It is not a saved replay: it is never listed and only travels inside a crash report.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.COLLECT.d: Reason, logs and system info always. A crash adds the backtrace, a full system scan and the recording; a clean exit uses a light snapshot (memory and this process only) so closing stays fast. DxDiag is never put in the zip.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.REDACT.de: A redactor learns every secret BMM stores (data.json, the BetterCommunity key file, the snapshot and dump) and scrubs each entry before it is written: text, JSON fields and the recording's bytes. A redaction.txt note marks the zip as clean.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.ZIP.desc: crash_<date>.zip goes to Reports/Crash, session_<date>.zip to Reports/Session. Only the 5 newest stay there; older ones move to Archive/, which keeps 20 per kind.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.OLD_REPOR: Once per start, in the background, every zip without the redaction note (written by an older BMM) is rewritten through the redactor, DxDiag dropped, its date kept. It pauses behind deploys and games and resumes next start.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.NOTICE.de: On the next launch, the backend's flag or a crash_ zip newer than the last one shown opens the crash notice (a step of the launch deck). The same crash is announced once.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.MANAGER.d: The Settings manager lists, analyses, opens, exports and deletes report zips and saved recordings. Only zips inside BMM's own crash folder can be read or deleted from there.
Report this crash opens the feedback dialog on the crash tab with the zip pre-attached; any recent zip can be ticked. A fresh DxDiag is attached only when its box is ticked.
docs.diagram.crash-reporting.n.LIVE.desc: Only with telemetry consent and the live errors switch on: the panic is redacted, grouped by fingerprint, queued on disk and sent to the telemetry service's /issues on this or the next launch.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.title: Custom pages: permissions and sandbox
docs.diagram.custom-pages.summary: How a custom page gets its permissions (an imported page starts with none), how it is served, and how every request it makes is checked again in Rust.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.IMPORT.desc: A shared navbar file can carry pages with the permissions and sites they held on the machine that exported them. The importer treats those as requests, never as grants.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.PENDING.desc: create_imported_custom_page always creates a NEW page, with empty grants and no sites, in the import-pending state. Only known permissions and well-formed origins are recorded as requested, so re-importing a file can never raise an existing page's grants.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.REVIEW.desc: Lists what each page asks for, with one line on what it allows. Nothing starts ticked, and Grant none is the default answer: Enter, Escape, the close button and a click outside all mean none.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.APPLY.desc: page_apply_reviewed_grants only works on a page still pending, only accepts items the file asked for, and keeps sites only together with the network permission. If it fails, the page stays pending and holds nothing.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.EDITOR.desc: The user can grant or remove a permission and edit the allowed sites of a page at any time. On a page still pending, the first tick starts from nothing and drops the sites the file asked for.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.GRANTS.desc: Per page: grants.json (what it holds), net_origins.json (allowed sites) and grants_meta.json (how it got them). The effective grants are empty while an import awaits its review, whatever the files say. Six permissions exist: storage, notifications, network, read, clipboard and system.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.FRAME.desc: The page runs in an iframe without allow-same-origin, so its origin is opaque: no access to the BMM window, its DOM, invoke or cookies. It can only post messages to the app.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.PROTO.desc: Serves the page's own folder read-only: a path with .. is refused, then the resolved path must still be inside the folder. Each response carries a strict CSP: scripts from the bundle only, no frames, and network access only to the allowed sites when the page holds network.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.BROKER.desc: The only bridge. It identifies the page by the iframe that sent the message (never by what the page claims), and calls a fixed table of methods, never a generic invoke.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.GATE.desc: Checked in Rust on every call: the caller is not a page frame itself, the id is an installed page (no folder is created for an unknown id), and the permission is in its effective grants. The broker's cache can only say no without asking.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.DENIED.desc: The page receives an error and BMM shows which permission is missing, so the user knows what to grant.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.STORAGE.desc: A private key/value store per page (storage.json, 2 MB cap), anonymous system facts, and the notifications, clipboard and app info the broker serves itself once Rust has said yes.
docs.diagram.custom-pages.n.FETCH.desc: A plain GET to an allowed site only, without BMM's cookies or headers. Redirects are followed only to allowed sites, and the response is capped at 8 MB.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.summary: How a bmm:// link reaches BMM, the one gate every link passes (hard limits, then a dialog), and what the routes do once allowed.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.LINK.desc: From a web page, another program, a QR code. Any page can fire one and the browser does not say which, so a link is treated as input from a stranger. The route table (every action and the parameters it reads) is generated from the handler itself, and a check fails the build when it drifts.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.OS.desc: BMM claims the bmm:// scheme for its own executable (not when run from a temp folder). Only one instance runs: a link opened while BMM is up goes to the running window. At a cold start the link is kept until the window is ready and asks for it.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.TRUSTED.desc: A task you saved and a caller holding the API token use the same routes through a private entry point, as trusted origins: no dialog, since nobody is there to answer at 3 a.m. A theme button or anything calling the window function cannot claim to be trusted.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.HANDLER.desc: Parses the action and its parameters. When deep links are switched off in Plugins and API, every link is refused with a message. What reaches the session log has its passwords, keys and tokens masked.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.LIMITS.desc: Refused whatever you would answer: a program path (app/launch only takes a registered app id), a script payload, a non-https download, a network or relative path, a signing key or passphrase in the link, an app install with no sha256, an unknown catalogue or resources action.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.REFUSED.desc: A toast names the action and the reason. Nothing was read, fetched, written or run.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.ASK.desc: Anything that changes state, downloads, writes or runs shows one dialog with what will happen, the exact target and who asked; Cancel is the default. Navigation-only routes, and routes that open a screen with their own confirmation, skip it, as do trusted callers.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.ACT.desc: Once allowed: enable or disable a mod, activate a profile, apply a theme, follow a catalogue, run a task, restart, and so on, through the same commands the screens use.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.SCREEN.desc: Generating, updating or hosting a repo, a sync, a mod install or import open the matching screen with the fields filled in, and nothing runs until you confirm there.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.LINKCMD.desc: Installing an app, plugin or theme, launching an app and exporting the data file go through separate Rust commands that repeat the limits: https only, a matching sha256 for apps, a plugin lands disabled with no permissions, the exported data file is redacted.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.API.desc: Forwards a call to the local HTTP API with BMM's own API token, so the dialog is the protection: it is shown for every call from outside, GET included. The path must start with /api/; the other parameters become the query or the JSON body.
docs.diagram.deeplinks.n.RESULT.desc: A toast or the screen that opened says what happened, or the error. An action no route knows passes the gate and then does nothing: only the initial "Deep Link" notice shows.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.title: Discord Rich Presence
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.summary: When BMM updates your Discord status, what it shows, and where the buttons' links come from.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.SETTING.desc: Off by default. Switched from Settings, a bmm://discord/rpc link, the local API (POST /api/discord/rpc, carried out by the interface) or a scheduler step. The choice is saved in the settings of data.json.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.EVENTS.desc: After a profile switch, a mod toggle, or turning the setting on, the active profile's name and its number of active mods are sent in the interface's language. The Flappy Tasky mini game sets its own score line while it is open.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.INIT.desc: Called once at startup and whenever the setting is toggled. When the setting is on, it builds a first status from the active profile (fixed French text at this point) and sends it; when off, it returns without touching the connection.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.PRESENCE.desc: The only command that talks to Discord. It takes two lines of text, details and state, and decides itself whether anything is shown, so callers do not need to check the setting.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.ENABLED.desc: Read from the settings on every call. When it is off and a connection is open, the connection is closed, which clears the status on Discord.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.CONNECT.desc: Opened on first use with BMM's Discord application id and kept for the session. If Discord is not running the call fails with FAILED_TO_CONNECT and the next update tries again.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.LINKS.desc: Read from links.json on GitHub (2.5 second timeout), then the bundled copy, then built-in defaults. BoutonRPC1 and BoutonRPC2 pick which of two website and GitHub addresses the buttons use.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.ACTIVITY.desc: The two text lines, the BMM logo with the version and this installation's creator id as its tooltip, and two buttons: Website, with ?creator=<id> added to its address, and GitHub.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.NONE.desc: Setting off, or Discord not reachable. Turning the setting off from Settings does not close an open connection by itself: the status goes away at the next presence call or when BMM exits.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.CLIENT.desc: The Discord client running on the same machine, reached through its local IPC pipe. The status is handed over locally; Discord publishes it.
docs.diagram.discord-rpc.n.SHOWN.desc: Friends see Better Mods Manager with the profile and mod count lines and the two buttons, until the status changes or BMM closes.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.title: Resource governor: how BMM paces its disk work
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.summary: Every heavy operation takes a ticket, gets a policy for its disk from the preset and the per-disk rules, and copies through one shared speed limit per disk.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.PRESET.de: Quiet (one thread, low I/O priority, short pauses), Balanced (the default), Everything for BMM (parallelism by disk type, 4 MiB buffers, no pauses) or Custom. A scheduled task can set one for its own duration only (at most 2 hours). The one-click storage presets write a preset, rules and space alerts together, with a preview and an undo.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.RULES.des: Optional rules per disk and per kind of work: MB/s ceiling, operations at once, buffer size, I/O priority. The speed cap of Disks & space (typed, or suggested by the disk benchmark) is that disk's rule for every kind.
Every 5 seconds BMM looks for a running program from a profile's game folder or your list (or a full-screen game). While one runs, the Quiet preset is in force and the background kinds you chose (hashing, scans, downloads...) are paused; deploy, install and backup are only slowed, never held. It ends 30 seconds after the program closes by default.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.CONFIG.de: The preset, the rules per disk and per kind, the app list and the app mode options. Each change reconfigures the governor at once: queue slots and thread pools are rebuilt.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.TICKET.de: Each operation (Deploy, Backup, Install, Extract, Compress, Scan, Hash, Download, Image, Maintenance) holds a ticket while it runs. Tickets wait for a slot of their kind and are what Live activity lists, pauses and cancels. Background work steps aside while a deploy or an install runs.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.RESOLVE.d: Starts from the preset in force, then each field comes from the most specific rule: this disk and kind, this disk, any disk and this kind. The result is clamped (64 KiB to 16 MiB buffer, at most 16 at once, 256 MiB in flight). Under Balanced, a game or backup folder on the system drive gets one operation at a time.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.POOL.desc: Each kind has its own pool sized by the preset (Quiet one thread, Balanced two for deploys, Everything for BMM all cores but one) and never takes every core. Its threads run at the preset's priority, never above normal.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.FULL_SPEE: Smart I/O off, Balanced, no cap?
Only that combination skips the governed copy, as BMM always did with Smart I/O turned off. Any MB/s rule on the disk, or another preset, goes through the chunked copy.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.OS_COPY.d: The whole file is copied by the system in one call, as fast as the disks allow. The ticket is still checked before it starts.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.CHUNKS.de: Reads and writes the file in chunks of the policy's buffer size (128 KiB when a MB/s cap applies, 1 MiB under Balanced). Without a cap, Smart I/O yields 150 microseconds every 16 MiB so the window stays smooth. Low I/O priority is set on the file handles when the policy asks for it.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.LIMITER.d: Every chunk draws from the destination disk's budget, so two copies to one disk share one MB/s limit instead of each getting its own. A limit set for one kind only (say Download) has a budget of its own on that disk.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.CHECKPOIN: Before each chunk the ticket is checked: a pause waits there, a cancel stops the copy.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.DONE.desc: Bytes read and written are added to the ticket, which is what Live activity and the progress bars show. Every deployed file is a real copy: BMM never uses links.
docs.diagram.disk-io-limiter.n.CANCELLED: The partly written destination file is deleted, so a cancelled copy never leaves half a file behind.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.title: Running a repo server in Docker
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.summary: The Docker files BMM writes next to a standalone repo server, and what docker compose up builds and runs from them.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.CARD.de: In the Standalone server card, or the standalone server ticked inside a .zip export: server type, port (8000 by default), admin password, an optional download password, and the Docker box with the host system (Linux or Windows).
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.GEN.des: Writes the server files into the repo folder; it refuses a folder with no repo.json. BMM does not run Docker: everything after this happens on the machine you copy the folder to.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.KIND.de: Four Dockerfile templates: the Node server (node server.js) or the script server (the generated .sh or .bat), each for a Linux or a Windows host. The Node and script servers each have their own compose template.
Node: server.js, package.json and public/dashboard.html. Script: BMM-Standalone-Server.sh and .bat. Beside them access-gate.js, keyauth.mjs and an empty access.json, plus copies of bans.json and whitelist.json when BMM has them.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.DOCKERF: Linux: Node 22 on Alpine, pinned by version and digest, dumb-init, a non-root bmm user. Windows: Node is downloaded and checked against its SHA-256 in a Server Core stage, then runs on Nano Server as ContainerUser. Both expose the port and probe /repo.json as their health check.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.COMPOSE: One service, bmm-repo-server, publishing the port as is, restarted unless stopped, with its own health check every 30 seconds. It holds no password, so it can be shared or committed.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.ENV.des: ADMIN_PASSWORD, quoted so Compose reads it literally (a line break is refused), readable by its owner only on Linux and macOS. BMM adds .env to .gitignore and .dockerignore so it stays out of git and out of the image.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.UP.desc: Run in the repo folder. Builds the image with mods/, repo.json, Info.json and the server copied in (and npm install for the Node server), then starts the container.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.VOLUMES: mods/, repo.json and Info.json are mounted read-only from the folder, so a regenerated repo is served without rebuilding. server.log, history.json and downloads.json are mounted writable; bans.json and whitelist.json are writable for the Node server, read-only for the script.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.CONTAIN: Serves repo.json and the mods on the chosen port, as a non-root process; the admin panel answers only to ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env.
The generated files only publish the port on the host. Making it reachable from the internet (port forward, reverse proxy with HTTPS, a tunnel) is set up by you.
docs.diagram.docker-deployment.n.CLIENTS: BMM clients paste the address of repo.json and sync as from any other repo.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.title: Threads, pools and the worker process
docs.diagram.engine-threads.summary: Where BMM's work actually runs: the async runtime, governed thread pools, background threads, and a separate process for mod files.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.WEBVIEW.de: The interface's JavaScript runs on the webview's own thread and only waits on promises. WebView2 is started with its renderer processes capped at 2 and its unused browser features off.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.ASYNC.desc: Tauri's Tokio runtime runs the async commands and the local HTTP API. Anything that reads or writes files at length is moved to a blocking task, carrying the job's cancel scope with it.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.LOCK: One mod operation at a time
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.LOCK.desc: Enabling and disabling share one global lock (MOD_OP_LOCK), so two mod operations never write the game folder at once. A cancel that arrived while waiting for the lock is checked again before any work starts.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.BG.desc: Two named threads with 512 KB stacks at Windows background priority: lazy SHA hashing (starts 5 s after launch) and content-id filling (starts after 8 s, one mod at a time). They hold Hash and Maintenance tickets, so they wait while a deploy runs.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.TICKET.des: Every heavy operation takes a ticket of its kind (deploy, install, backup, extract, compress, scan, hash, download, image, maintenance). Each kind has a number of slots; hash and maintenance work steps aside while a deploy or install runs. Tickets are what the Storage Manager lists and can pause or cancel.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.GAME.desc: A sampler thread looks at the running executables every 5 s, against every profile's game folder and a manual list. While a game runs, the chosen kinds are paused and the others throttled; game mode ends 30 s (by default) after the game is gone.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.POOLS.desc: Each kind has its own rayon pool, sized by the preset and never using every core: Balanced gives hashing cores/2 (1 to 4), extraction and compression the size of the global pool, others 2. The global pool built at start is cpus-2 above 6 cores, with 512 KB stacks.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.DISK.desc: Copies go through the governed copy: one rate limiter per volume shared by every copy to that disk, with a pause and cancel checkpoint between chunks.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.SPAWN.desc: Writes the job to a JSON file in the temp folder and starts the same executable with --mod-worker, hidden (no console window) and at below-normal priority. It then polls the child every 1 to 50 ms, relaying its progress.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.WORKER.des: Starts without Tauri or the webview, drops itself to Windows background mode (CPU, disk and paging priority), and applies or removes the mod's files under the parent's governor rules. It prints its byte count every 100 ms and writes its result to a second JSON file.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.CANCEL.des: Cancel (from the job, the governor dashboard or Cancel all) kills the worker process, however stuck its disk I/O is. A second worker, which cannot be cancelled, then runs the inverse operation so no half-applied mod is left.
docs.diagram.engine-threads.n.PROGRESS.d: Progress reaches the window as bmm://mod-op-progress events, at most 10 per second, and the end of each mod as a done, failed or cancelled event. Each run also logs its duration and memory use to the crash log.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.title: A mod was deleted
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.summary: What happens to the game when a mod's folder disappears, and how to get the game files back in each case.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.IN_APP.de: The card's Remove action refuses an enabled mod ("disable it first"), in the screen and again in the backend. For a disabled mod you choose: remove it from the library only, or also delete its folder or archive. Other mods' dependencies on it are dropped.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.SAFE.desc: A disabled mod has no file in the game folder, so deleting it, in BMM or in Explorer, leaves the game exactly as it was.
The mod's folder or archive was deleted in Explorer (or by another tool) while the mod was enabled. Its files are still in the game folder and the card still shows it as enabled.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.SCANNED.d: A Scan, the automatic scan when the list refreshes, a scheduled scan or the mapper's rescan all remove entries whose folder is gone, as long as the drive holding the mods folder is connected.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.VERIFY.de: Checks the enabled mods of the profile. For a mod with hashes whose folder is gone, each file is reported as missing in the library. A mod without hashes is not reported this way.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.DISABLE.d: Disabling works without the mod's folder: it uses the list of files recorded when the mod was enabled. Each file gets back the copy of the next mod that ships it, or the original from _original/, or is deleted if the game never had it.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.CLEAN.des: The game is back to what it would be without that mod. You can then remove the entry, or let the next scan do it.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.PRUNED.de: The mod is removed from the library and from the active profile's active list, together with its record of installed files. The scan does not touch the game folder.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.LEFT.desc: The mod's files are still in the game folder and the originals they replaced are still in the profile's _original/ backup, but nothing links them to a mod any more.
Restore the folder or archive (from the recycle bin, or download it again) into the mods folder and run a Scan. It comes back as a new, disabled entry.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.CYCLE.des: Enabling records the files again. An existing backup is never overwritten, so the true originals in _original/ are kept, and disabling puts them back.
docs.diagram.faq-deleted-mod.n.ADDED_LEF: A file the mod ADDED (the game never had it) has no backup, so on that enable BMM takes the leftover copy for a game file and keeps it on disable. Delete those files from the game folder yourself, using the mod's folder as the list.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.title: My disk is filling up
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.summary: What BMM checks before it writes, what happens when a disk fills during a copy, where the space goes and where to see it.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.ENABLE.desc: From a toggle, an order list or a modpack. The checks below run once per mod, before any file is written.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.ROOM.desc: The mod's total size plus a 500 MB margin must be free on the game folder's disk and on the backup folder's disk. Otherwise the mod is refused with the size it needs.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.ALERTS.desc: Off by default (Storage Manager, Disks & space). When on, BMM computes the free share left after this mod: at or below the critical threshold (30% by default) the mod is refused; at or below the warning one (40%) it goes in with a warning.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.REFUSED.des: Nothing was copied. The card turns back off and the message names the disk and the space needed.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.COPY.desc: For each file, the original is backed up, then the mod's file is copied, in a separate worker process under the governor's rules. A backup copy that fails is skipped without an error, so the space check above is what keeps the originals safe.
If the disk fills anyway (another program wrote meanwhile), the copy stops with the system error and the mod is not marked as enabled. Unlike a Cancel, nothing is undone automatically: files already copied stay in the game folder. In crash reports, Laya can label this error as disk full.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.ON.desc: The list of files written is recorded on the mod, and a space warning is shown if the alerts asked for one.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.DEPLOYED.de: Every enabled mod's files are real copies in the game folder: BMM never uses links. Two profiles on two game folders each hold their own copy.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.ORIGINALS.d: Each game file a mod replaced is kept once in _original/. The copy is deleted when the original goes back into the game.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.EXTRACTED.d: An archived mod is extracted once to %TEMP%\bmm_mod_cache before it can be enabled. BMM does not clear this folder; Windows' temporary file cleanup can.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.SESSIONS.de: Saved replays and session reports are pruned to your limits: 30 sessions and 2 GB by default, set in Crash reports and sessions.
docs.diagram.faq-disk-full.n.STORAGE.des: Settings, Storage: each disk's used and free space, which profiles keep their game, mods or backup folder on it, a speed cap and the space alerts.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.title: Publishing a repo
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.summary: The three ways to build a signed repo.json, the four ways to serve it, and the access rules a server can apply.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.g.BUILD: Build the repo (Server Repo, Host tab)
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.PICK.desc: Choose the profiles (and modpacks) to share, the author name shown to subscribers and the output folder. The Host tab then offers three alternative ways to produce the manifest.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.EXPORT.desc: Copies every mod into mods/ (or packs each one as mods/<id>.zip with "zip mods") and hashes each file with its 4 MB chunks. "Compress as .zip" packs the whole repo; the compression method (Deflate, Zstandard, Bzip2, Stored) applies to both. Can also write a standalone server beside it.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.MANIFEST.des: Writes just repo.json for mod folders already on this machine (folders, profiles or both), copying nothing. A layout template such as {id}/{path} lets an existing server keep its own folder shape.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.REFRESH.desc: Reads what the server already holds, from its HTTP directory listing or over SFTP, and writes the manifest without pulling the repo back. A dry run first says what it would add, change and remove.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.SIGN.desc: The manifest is signed with this BMM's ed25519 key (created on first use): author_id is the public key, signature covers the whole manifest. Re-running keeps the repo's seed, so subscribers' salted ids stay the same.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.FOLDER.desc: The repo folder: repo.json (files, sizes, SHA-256, chunk hashes, signature), Info.json with statistics after a full export, and the mods/ folder. Adding anything to repo.json after signing breaks the signature, and subscribers refuse it.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.ACCESS.desc: Open by default. A download password (sent as X-Repo-Password or ?password=), authorised public keys (a signed proof becomes required for everyone), a required BetterCommunity login, and the ban list and whitelist restrict it. The admin password only protects a standalone server's admin panel.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.BUILTIN.desc: Serves the folder from BMM itself on the chosen port, on every interface (LAN address). It asks the router for a UPnP port forward (public address) and starts a cloudflared quick tunnel (a random trycloudflare.com address; cloudflared is downloaded into the app data folder on first use unless a path to your own is set). Stopping removes both.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.STANDALONE.d: Generates a server to run without BMM, next to repo.json: a Node server (server.js, package.json, dashboard) or a .bat/.sh script, plus access.json, and optionally Docker files.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.HUB.desc: One Node server and dashboard for several repo folders, or a static index (index.html and hub-repos.json) to drop on any web host.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.SSH.desc: Uploads the folder to the SSH target saved in the panel, repo.json last, so a subscriber syncing during the upload sees the old repo or the new one, never half of it. Any static web server can then serve it.
docs.diagram.hosting-flow.n.LINK.desc: Subscribers paste the address of repo.json in Server Repo, Sync. HTTPS is strongly recommended for anything outside your network.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.title: Translation (i18n) system
docs.diagram.i18n-system.summary: How a key becomes text on screen: language files on disk, every language loaded at start, then the active language, French, or the raw key.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.LANGFILES.des: One flat key-to-text JSON per language in the Lang folder shipped with the app, with an _info entry (name, flag) and optional _synonyms. template.json is never listed as a language. A build gate requires en.json and fr.json to hold exactly the same keys.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.LOAD.desc: get_available_languages lists every .json in the folder except the template (fr and en when it is empty); get_language_content returns one file's raw text.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.MANAGE.desc: A new language is created from scratch or as a copy of another, or imported from a file (also by deeplink or the local API). en, fr and template can never be deleted, and a language code may only hold letters, digits, - and _.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.RUST_KEYS.des: Rust commands report most user-facing errors as a key, such as repo.errNoExistingRepo, and the interface passes it to t(). A build gate checks that every such key in the Rust code exists in both languages.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.INIT.desc: At start, initI18n reads the saved language (French by default) and loads every language file in parallel into memory, splitting off _info and _synonyms. A language imported or deleted from Settings is picked up without a restart.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.T.desc: The one lookup every string goes through, hundreds of times per render. It fills {placeholders} in a single pass without regular expressions. Custom tutorial texts (ctut.* keys) are consulted only on a miss.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.CUR.desc: The active language's dictionary is tried first. An empty value counts as missing.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.FRFALL.desc: French is the base language: a key missing from the active language falls back to fr.json.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.SANDBOX.desc: A Settings tool to browse and edit every key, see where it is used, find hardcoded text and create a language. Its edits are an in-memory overlay that t() reads first, so they show everywhere at once; closing it clears them, and Export downloads the finished .json.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.SYN.desc: The _synonyms groups of every loaded language merge into one map, which widens queries in the command palette and in the docs hub's search.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.SWITCH.desc: Picking a language in Settings calls setLang: it saves the choice in the settings, repaints the page and fires a langChanged event that dynamic screens listen to. No restart.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.DOM.desc: Fills every element carrying data-i18n, data-i18n-placeholder, -title, -content or -tooltip. An icon-only button also gets its tooltip text as its accessible name.
