docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.TEXT.desc: The text shown, with its placeholders filled in.
docs.diagram.i18n-system.n.RAWKEY.desc: Last resort: the key itself appears, so a missing translation is visible and easy to report instead of silent.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.title: Integrity engine
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.summary: How BMM records a hash baseline for each mod, checks a mod against it, and what "require valid SHA" does when a mod has none.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.QUEUE.de: Mods with no hashes yet join the normal queue when "Hash new mods in the background" is on (populate_sha_queue), or through Recalculate hashes (only missing, or everything). A mod whose last check failed is not re-queued automatically.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.PRIORITY: Enabling a mod that has no hashes moves it from the normal queue to the priority queue, so it is hashed next. Only while background hashing is on.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.WORKER.d: One low-priority background thread: priority queue first, one mod at a time, a short pause between mods, under a Hash ticket of the disk governor. A manual Re-hash runs the same code on its own thread. A cancelled run, or an unplugged drive, keeps the old hashes.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.BASELINE: One BLAKE3 hash per file (written b3:..., older baselines are SHA-256) and the time it was taken, saved in data.json. Archived mods are hashed from their extracted view, so they match their unzipped twin.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.CENTER.d: Sorts mods into four states: verified, mismatch, missing (no baseline) and not checked. Verify runs one mod after another, skips mods with no hash, and Stop takes effect between two mods.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.VERIFY.d: Re-reads one mod on a blocking thread under a Hash ticket, so it can be paused or cancelled. A mod with no baseline gets one here instead and is reported valid: only a later check can fail.
Each recorded file is re-hashed with the algorithm its stored hash names. Files that are gone count as missing, files that changed as modified, and new files as added.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.VERIFIED: Nothing missing, modified or added: isValid is true, the mismatch flag is cleared and the row shows as verified.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.MISMATCH: The failed result is saved on the mod (file_hashes_invalid), so the warning icon survives a restart. Re-hashing a mismatched mod asks for confirmation first, because its current files become the new reference.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.ENABLE.d: Before any file is copied, the activation checks every mod it is about to enable, dependencies included.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.STRICT.d: With the "require valid SHA" setting on, a mod with no hashes stops the activation with a MISSING_SHA error, unless the caller passed the bypass. The setting is off by default.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.ASK.desc: The library asks: hash the mod now and leave it off, or enable it anyway (a retry with the bypass). Closing the question leaves the mod off.
docs.diagram.integrity-engine.n.ACTIVATE: The free-space checks and the file copy run as shown in the activation diagram.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.title: Launch packs: build and run
docs.diagram.launch-packs.summary: How a list of programs becomes a hidden launcher script and a shortcut, and what running a pack really does.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.EDITOR.desc: A name, the programs (.exe, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .lnk) picked from disk or from the installed-apps list read from the Windows uninstall registry keys, and an optional icon.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.IMPORT.desc: Reads a .bmmlaunch file: refused if it is not a launch pack or lists more than 64 programs. The icon is re-encoded, never written as is, and the programs whose path does not exist on this PC are named, not dropped. The pack is then built here like a new one.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.SAVE.desc: Regenerates the pack's machine-specific files in LaunchPacks/<id> in BMM's data folder and records the pack. It runs off the main thread.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.ICON.desc: The chosen image is resized to 256x256 and saved as icon.ico, under an Image ticket of the resource governor.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.EXPORT.desc: Writes a .bmmlaunch: the name, the program paths and the icon inlined (up to 4 MB). The launcher and the shortcut are not included: their paths only mean something on this PC.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.DATA.desc: Id, name, program paths, icon path and creation date. Included in .DATABMM backups.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.VBS.desc: One WshShell.Run line per program, window hidden and without waiting: a .ps1 through PowerShell with a hidden window, anything else through cmd start.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.LNK.desc: A shortcut to the launcher with the pack's icon, written in the pack's folder (Open folder shows it, ready to copy to the desktop). The name is cleaned so it can never point outside that folder.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.TRIGGER.desc: The Run button on the card, a bmm://launchpack/run link, a scheduled task action or the MCP server all start the same launcher.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.RUN_CMD.desc: Finds the pack and its folder (a folder name that is not a plain id is refused).
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.HAS_VBS.desc: The only check made at run time. Whether each program still exists is not checked.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.MISSING.desc: An error is shown; saving the pack again regenerates the launcher.
docs.diagram.launch-packs.n.APPS.desc: wscript runs the launcher with no console window. BMM does not wait for the programs or report their errors: a program that fails to start fails silently.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.title: Laya on crash reports
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.summary: How Laya groups crash reports, proposes a probable cause with its evidence, and helps while a report is written. Local engines only.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.g.LABEL: Probable cause (on click)
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.MANAG: When the manager lists crash reports, a Laya strip is added above the list if Laya may run. With AI off it draws nothing.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.DIGES: For up to 60 reports, builds a short excerpt: the reason, what the window recorded, the first stack frames that are not runtime plumbing, the last error lines of the log. User names, PC name, e-mails and IPs are masked in Rust before anything is returned.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.OFF.d: Master switch off, --no-ai, or a classifier that is not local (BetterCommunity): the call is refused and no report is read for Laya. A crash log is never sent to a server for this.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.GROUP: Reports whose reason matches once numbers, addresses and paths are set aside share a group badge; clicking it shows only that group. Grouping is plain text comparison, no model.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.LABEL: ai_crash_label
On the user's click, one representative report per group is labelled, 12 per call, newest first. If the engine fails on the first report the whole call stops with its reason.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.CACHE: Answers are cached in memory per report and per answer settings (up to 200), so reopening the manager costs nothing. The debug panel can clear the cache.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.QUEST: One model call with short questions: which family (mod files, game, disk, network, window, engine, Laya, updater, memory, unknown), then which cause inside each family that has several. Small questions instead of one listing all 19 causes.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.BLEND: Family and cause probabilities are combined, then mixed with keyword evidence from the excerpt at a quarter weight. Keywords alone decide only when Laya gave nothing.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.DECID: The Crash reports answer settings apply: threshold, margin and temperature. Below them, the cause reads unknown, or the best guess is shown flagged as uncertain, as the user chose.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.CHIPS: Each report of a group gets the label with its confidence, the keywords and log lines that back it (paths masked) and a fixed next step. Family chips, then cause chips, filter the list with counts.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.TASKS: New labels are announced as events a scheduled task can wait for; a task can also label crashes itself through the same engine and gate.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.EXPLA: Drawn only when a generator is configured; a remote one is named on the button before the click. The answer is shown as untrusted markdown: no images, embeds or anything that fetches.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.GENER: A server on this PC or a remote API the user chose receives the masked excerpt only, and returns at most four short sentences: the likely cause and one or two things to try.
docs.diagram.laya-crash-analysis.n.FEEDB: While a report is written, Laya proposes its kind and app area, and the crash zip on this PC that fits the description. Each proposal is applied with a click; while typing it runs only on a local engine.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.title: Laya, the local AI classifier
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.summary: How a Laya feature runs: the gate, the questions, the three engines, the answer settings, the optional generator and what reaches you.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.SETTINGS.de: One Settings card opens the Laya dialog: Overview (the master switch, the model, where it runs, what leaves the PC), Requirement (how sure Laya must be), My tasks, and For programs (the local API). Choices are saved in ai-settings.json; the master switch is off by default.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.FEATURES.de: Suggest in a mod's panel, Analyse the library, Ask Laya and the smart library search, the hints of the feedback dialog and the crash causes. Each runs on the user's click or while a report is typed, never in the background on its own.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.PROGRAMS.de: Scheduled tasks and scripts, the local API (127.0.0.1, with a token) and the CLI/MCP use the same engine. They wait while a game runs, share one engine slot and are capped at 30 calls a minute; what they get back is data, never applied.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.EXTRACT.des: Name, version, author, description and links come from the mod's manifest, readme and similar files, in folders and .zip archives. Always offline, no model involved, and it runs even with AI off.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.GATE.desc: The only place a provider is chosen. It refuses when --no-ai or BMM_NO_AI is set, the master switch is off, the feature is off, or no provider is configured; BetterCommunity also needs the user's consent. While no classifier was picked, an installed embedded model is the default.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.BLOCKED.des: A short reason (killed, ai_off, feature_off, no_provider, no_consent) is returned and shown; no model is loaded and no request is made.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.QUESTIONS.d: Tags become descriptive criteria in ten languages, keywords pre-filter the candidates to at most 10 options plus none, and only the informative lines of a text are kept. Every text is masked and neutralised first, so it cannot forge an option.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.EMBEDDED.de: The laya-multilingual model run in-process through ONNX Runtime: no Python, no server, no network. Loaded on the first question with 2 threads, dropped again after 5 minutes without one.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.PACK.desc: About 327 MB, from the installer (models/laya next to BMM) or downloaded from the Laya dialog to the local app data folder. Its SHA-256 and file hashes are pinned in the code, the lock file and the installer; check-laya-pins fails when they drift.
The user's own Laya server, 127.0.0.1:8000 by default. Only loopback unless remote is explicitly allowed; its key is bound to that address.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.BC.desc: Only for mod suggestions and the report hint, and only after the user accepted what is sent (at most 4000 characters). Never used for tasks, report assist, crash causes or Ask.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.TUNING.desc: Per area (suggest, Ask, reports, library, tasks, API, crashes): temperature, threshold, margin between the top two, and on a refusal either I don't know or a guess flagged as uncertain. Balanced is the built-in behaviour.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.GENERATOR.d: Only when the user configured one (Ollama-style server on this PC, or a remote API with their key): a description draft, a written Ask answer, a crash explanation. Its output is checked for links, paths and commands not in the sources, and Laya must agree it is supported, or it is dropped.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.CALL_LOG.de: An in-memory ring of the last 50 model calls: feature, provider, latency, outcome, decision. No question, report or user label is kept. The debug menu's Laya panel reads it, with the engine state and a raw tester.
docs.diagram.laya-pipeline.n.PROPOSALS.d: Each row shows its source and confidence and starts unticked. Apply writes only the ticked fields, validated again in Rust; tags are only ever the user's existing ones, at most 3 per mod.
docs.diagram.lightweight-architecture.su: What "Generate the server" writes next to your repo.json, and how that small Node server then serves subscribers without BMM running.
Standalone server card
Port, version (v1 or v2), type, admin password, upload limit, Cloudflare tunnel, UPnP, autostart and Docker. The target is the repo.json path, or the host or export folder when that field is empty.
generate_standalone_server
Refuses if no repo.json exists at that path, then writes every file into the folder that holds it. Nothing is compiled: the server is text files filled in from templates bundled in BMM.
Server type?
User (simple) writes one self-contained script per OS. Server (dedicated Node.js) writes an Express app; for that type the Cloudflare, UPnP and autostart options are switched off in the form.
BMM-Standalone-Server .bat / .sh

A polyglot file: a batch or shell header that finds Node.js, then the JavaScript server in the same file. Without Node it downloads a pinned Node.js 22 binary and checks its SHA-256 before running it. v1 (Std) or v2 (Lux) templates.
Express server

server.js, package.json, public/dashboard.html and start scripts that run npm install then npm start, so Node.js and npm must already be installed. The download password typed in the form is written into server.js.
Access gate

access-gate.js and keyauth.mjs (the same verifier BetterCommunity runs, kept identical by a build check) plus a starter access.json: download password, authorised public keys and audience. An existing access.json is never overwritten.
bans.json and whitelist.json

BMM's current ban list and allow list are copied next to the server, if they exist. The server rereads them on each check and its own dashboard edits them; later changes made in BMM are not pushed to it.
Docker files
Only when Docker is ticked: a Dockerfile for a Linux or Windows host and a docker-compose.yml, with the admin password in a .env beside them instead of in the compose file.
Windows autostart
Only when ticked, and only on Windows: a BMM-Mini-Server value in the current user's Run registry key points at the .bat. Generating again without it removes that value.
Node.js server

Runs on any machine, BMM not needed. Each content request passes the access gate, the ban list and the whitelist. The User script can also open a Cloudflare tunnel or a UPnP port mapping, downloading the tool it needs.
repo.json, mods and dashboard

Serves repo.json and the mod files, a public /dashboard and /monitoring.json, and /admin/data, /admin/update, /admin/logs and /admin/monitoring behind the admin password, compared in constant time. The v1 script also writes monitoring.json to disk, which BMM's monitoring table adds when it serves that same folder.
Subscribers sync over HTTP

Other BMM users add the server's address in Server Repo. BMM fetches repo.json with the X-Repo-Password header and a signed key proof when it has one, and reports a refusal as banned, not whitelisted or password required.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.title: MCP server and CLI
docs.diagram.mcp-server.summary: One executable, two front doors: an MCP server for AI clients and a command line for scripts, both reading BMM's files directly and reaching the running app through its local API.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.g.APP: BMM's data and the running app
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.AI_CLIENT.desc: Claude, or any client speaking the Model Context Protocol, starts the executable itself and talks JSON-RPC over its standard input and output. Logs go to standard error so they never mix with the protocol.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.TERMINAL.desc: The same executable with a subcommand (78 of them: profiles, mods, enable, sync, schedules, bmms-compile, api...), for a .bat file, a shell script or a CI job.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.EXE.desc: Built as a cargo example rather than a binary, so the installer bundler does not pick it up twice, and shipped next to BMM as a sidecar. No subcommand, or serve, starts MCP mode; anything else runs the CLI.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.MCP.desc: 92 tools today (profiles, mods, mod order, repos, catalogs, launch packs, crash reports, schedules, themes, translations, Laya and more), each declared once and dispatched once. check-mcp-tools.mjs fails the build on a duplicate, a missing arm, or a schedule tool description that names a trigger type that does not exist.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.CLI.desc: Each subcommand prints a readable result, and calls the same functions as the matching tool. JSON arguments can come from a file, from standard input, or inline.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.OFFLINE.desc: Reads and writes BMM's data folder (%APPDATA%/com.bettermm.desktop, or BMM_DATA_DIR) without the app: listing profiles and mods, toggling a mod's state in data.json, schedules, run logs, crash reports. This is why most tools answer with BMM closed.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.SHARED.desc: The BMMScript compiler, the run log reader, plugin asset reading and Laya (the same embedded model, offline) are the app's own source files mounted into the executable, not copies, so the CLI and the app cannot disagree.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.LIVE.desc: For actions only the running app can do (repo sync, modpacks, mod order, running a task, signals). The target is fixed to 127.0.0.1 and the configured API port, only /api/ paths and GET or POST, with the admin token read from data.json. If BMM is not running the call says so.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.DATA.desc: data.json (profiles, mods, settings with the API port and token), schedules.json, TaskRuns, crash reports, apps_state.json, plus the Lang and docs files the translation and documentation tools read.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.API.desc: BMM's own API server (port 51274 by default). Every request needs a bearer token: the admin token has full access, a plugin's token only the scopes granted to it, and the routes that edit those grants accept the admin token only.
docs.diagram.mcp-server.n.APP_UI.desc: Some actions (repo sync, repo generation, hosting, Discord presence) are handed to the interface as a bmm://api-exec event and performed the way a person would: the form is filled and the button pressed, with the usual progress and toasts.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.title: Mod activation and deactivation
docs.diagram.mod-activation.summary: How a toggle becomes a background job, and what happens to each game file when a mod goes on or off.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.START.desc: Every way of turning mods on or off (a card toggle, an order list, a modpack, a scheduled task) creates a job owned by the app, not by the screen. Leaving the view does not stop it.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.QUEUE.desc: Jobs run one after another, one mod at a time, each with its own cancel scope. Progress arrives as bmm://mod-op-progress events and shows on the cards and in the activity pill. A job refuses to run if its profile is no longer the active one.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.CANCEL.des: Only an explicit Cancel stops a job (activity pill, toolbar or keyboard). It cancels that job's scope only: the mod in flight is undone by the worker's inverse operation, mods not reached yet are left as they were.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.ENABLE.des: Resolves the dependency chain, then checks before touching anything: hashes present when "require valid SHA" is on, enough free space on the game and backup disks, and the mod not already active in another profile on the same game folder. Archived mods are extracted to a cache first.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.OWNED: Is the game file a mod's?
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.OWNED.desc: For each file, BMM asks whether the file currently in the game folder was put there by a mod, from any profile that uses this game folder. Only a real game original gets backed up.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.BACKUP.des: The vanilla file is copied once into the profile's backup folder under _original/, the first time any mod replaces it. An existing backup is never overwritten.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.COPY.desc: The mod's files are copied over (last enabled wins), in parallel under the disk governor's Deploy rules, with a cancel checkpoint between files. The list of files written becomes the mod's installed_files.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.DISABLE.de: Collects the files to take back (what was installed plus what the mod folder holds now) and the mods that stay, in activation order, including mods another profile enabled on the same game folder.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.PROVIDER.d: Deployment is last-wins, so the fallback is the LAST remaining mod (in activation order) that has this file: the layer directly under the one leaving.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.RESTORE_MO: The surviving mod's version is copied back into the game folder. Archived providers are read from their extracted cache.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.ORIGINAL.d: Looks for the vanilla file in this profile's _original/ first, then in the backups of the other profiles on the same game folder (the profile that replaced it first is the one that saved it).
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.RESTORE_OR: The original is copied back and its backup copy is removed to save space. Empty folders left behind are cleaned up.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.DELETE.des: No mod and no original: the file was added by this mod, so it is simply removed from the game folder.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.CASCADE.de: Dependencies this mod pulled in, and that no remaining active mod still requires, are disabled in turn. A dependency shared with another enabled mod stays.
docs.diagram.mod-activation.n.SAVED.desc: data.json is saved even when the chain stops part-way, the history logs the change, and a done/failed/cancelled event reaches the job so the card and the end toast tell the truth.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.title: Mod data model
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.summary: What a mod is on disk, what BMM records about it in data.json, and the in-memory views the rest of the app reads.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.FOLDER.d: A folder in the profile's mods folder whose tree mirrors the game's: each relative path is where that file lands in the game folder. BMM only changes it through the Mapper or a mod update.
A .zip, .7z, .rar, .tar or .tar.gz kept as one file. Its file list comes from the archive's own index, without extracting, and gives the same content_id as the unpacked twin.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.XCACHE.d: When an archived mod's files must really be read, it is extracted once to the system temp folder under bmm_mod_cache, keyed by name, size and date so a changed archive gets a fresh copy. Extraction is capped (16 GiB, and a 1000x expansion ratio past 64 MiB).
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.READ_ROO: The one place that answers "where are this mod's files?": the folder itself, or the archive's extraction cache. Activation, conflicts, integrity and the Mapper all go through it.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.ENTRY.de: One record per mod: id, name, path to the folder or archive, version, author, tags, dependencies, update sources, status, and the cached file list with the folder date it was taken at.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.IDENTITY: id is local to this install. content_id is stable across machines: the id in a bmm.json at the mod root, or a SHA-256 of its sorted paths and sizes. Mods from a repo also keep source_repo and repo_mod_id, which survive version bumps.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.HASHES.d: Relative path to content hash, BLAKE3 tagged b3: (older untagged values are read as SHA-256), plus when they were taken and whether the last check failed. Filled by the background hasher.
Three folders (game, mods, backup) and active_mods, the ordered list of enabled mod ids, which is also the deployment order. A mod belongs to a profile because its path is under that profile's mods folder, not through a stored id.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.FILES.de: Each mod's set of relative paths and, for each path, the mods that ship it. Rebuilt lazily from the saved lists; conflicts and the order view read it.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.WIRE.des: The Library gets a trimmed copy: enabled and position computed from the active profile, conflicts attached, and the big arrays (file list, installed files, hashes) left out. A feature that needs the hashes asks for one mod's.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.INSTALLE: Enabling copies the mod's files into the game folder and records them as installed_files on the entry, which is what disabling takes back.
docs.diagram.mod-architecture.n.BACKUP.d: Game files a mod replaced are copied once into the profile's backup folder under _original/, with the same relative path, and restored when no mod provides that file any more.
docs.diagram.mod-import.title: Adding a mod
docs.diagram.mod-import.summary: What happens when you add a folder or an archive: where it is copied, how an archive is kept zipped, and when it gets its hashes.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.DIALOG.desc: Opened from the Library (Add a mod, or Ctrl+M). You pick a folder or an archive (zip, 7z, rar, tar, tar.gz) and give a name, version, author, description, a tag and dependencies. The name is filled from the archive's file name when it is empty.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.DROP.desc: Dropping a folder or an archive onto the window while the Library is shown (and no dialog is open) opens the same dialog with the first dropped path and its name already filled. Nothing is copied before you confirm.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.OTHER.desc: A one-click install link downloads the mod, a shared mod list installs many at once, and a Scan picks up folders or archives you put in the mods folder yourself. Each ends with the same kind of library entry.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.ADD.desc: Copies into the mods folder of the ACTIVE profile. It refuses a source that is neither a folder nor a known archive, and does nothing when the source already is the target.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.KIND.desc: Decided from the file extension: .zip, .7z, .rar, .tar, .tar.gz and .tgz are archives, a directory is a folder mod.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.KEEP_ZIP.desc: The archive file is copied whole, never unpacked here. Its name becomes "Name.zip", or "Name (1).zip" when that is taken. It is extracted to a cache only when its files are actually read (activation, mapper, integrity).
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.COPY_DIR.desc: The folder's content, empty sub-folders included, goes into a new folder named after the mod. If that name exists, a suffix is added (Name_1, shown as "Name (1)"), so an existing mod is never overwritten.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.TICKET.desc: The copy runs off the UI thread as one Install operation of the disk governor: listed in the Storage Manager, paced by its rules, and cancellable between files. A cancelled copy removes what it had written.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.ENTRY.desc: A new mod record is saved, disabled, with a content_id (from a bmm.json id, or a fingerprint of its file paths and sizes) and the details from the dialog. The file cache is invalidated so conflicts are recomputed.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.HASH.desc: Adding does not hash. The mod gets its BLAKE3 baseline from the throttled background queue the next time it is filled (start-up, a Scan that found mods, a profile change), if lazy hashing is on in the settings.
docs.diagram.mod-import.n.LISTED.desc: The list refreshes and the new card appears switched off, with its conflict badges. Nothing has touched the game folder yet: that only happens when you enable it.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.title: Mapper: reshape a mod
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.summary: How the Mapper lays a mod's files out to mirror the game folder: a draft of moves, a preview, then changes written inside the mod only.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.MOD_TREE.desc: The selected mod's files, from the profile you pick. An archived mod is shown from its extracted cache, so it can be browsed without unpacking it for good. The walk is one Scan operation of the disk governor.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.GAME_TREE.desc: The profile's game folder, read only. It is the shape the mod has to mirror: a file at Data/Textures/x.dds in the mod lands at Data/Textures/x.dds in the game.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.PICK.desc: Select items in the mod tree, then double-click a folder of the game tree to move them there. With nothing selected, the whole mod (every top-level item) is moved. The root entry stands for the game root.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.QUEUE.desc: Moves, new folders and deletions are queued as a draft and shown in the mod tree as they will be. The Save button counts all three. Rename is the exception: it is written at once.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.PREVIEW.desc: Where every file will land in the game folder, grouped by top folder: new files, files that would overwrite a game file, files dropped at the game root, and how many files other mods share with this one. Save can be pressed from here.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.ARCHIVED.desc: An archive cannot be edited in place. BMM asks whether to zip it again after the changes or to keep it as a folder; cancelling keeps the whole draft and writes nothing.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.UNPACK.desc: The archive is extracted to a temporary folder beside it, renamed into place, and only then deleted; the mod record now points at the folder. A failed extraction leaves the archive as it was.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.APPLY.desc: In this order: create the new folders, move the items, delete the marked ones. A move into an existing folder MERGES and only replaces the files it lands on, and empty folders left behind are removed.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.REZIP.desc: Only when you chose to keep it zipped: the folder is packed beside itself and removed. Always as .zip: BMM reads 7z and rar but cannot write them, which the dialog says beforehand.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.MOD_DIR.desc: Every write happens inside the mod in the mods folder, never in the game folder. The file cache is invalidated so conflicts and the next activation see the new layout.
docs.diagram.mod-mapper.n.READY.desc: The mod now mirrors the game's tree. Enabling it is what copies its files into the game. If it was already enabled, disable and enable it again so the game gets the new layout.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.title: Scan and library index
docs.diagram.mod-sync.summary: How a Scan reconciles the library with the mods folder, and how the file index behind conflicts stays current without re-reading every mod.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.TRIGGER.desc: The Scan button in the Library, an automatic scan when the list is refreshed after a profile or link action (at most once per interval, 30 seconds by default, set in the settings), a scheduled task, or the mapper when it finds a new mod. It scans the active profile's mods folder.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.GONE.desc: Every library entry is checked first. A missing folder or archive only counts as deleted when the mods folder that holds it is reachable right now.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.KEEP.desc: If the whole mods folder is missing (external drive unplugged or given another letter), its mods are kept with their hashes and activation state, so plugging the drive back restores everything instead of re-adding blank entries.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.PRUNE.desc: An entry whose folder is gone, or whose path is under no profile's mods folder any more, is removed from the library and from the active profile's active list. Files it had deployed in the game folder are not touched.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.WALK.desc: Reads the top level of the mods folder as one Scan operation of the disk governor (pausable, cancellable between entries). Each sub-folder and each archive is a candidate mod; loose files are ignored, and paths already in the library are skipped.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.NEW.desc: A new mod is created from the folder or archive name (archive extension removed), with a content_id, switched off. The scan never modifies a file in the mods folder.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.DATA.desc: Saved when anything was added or removed; the in-memory file index is marked stale. The toast reports how many mods were added and removed.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.POPULATE.desc: Done lazily, the next time the mod list or the conflicts are read, not by the scan itself. It never extracts an archive and releases its locks before any hashing, so a big library does not freeze the window.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.MTIME.desc: Compares the modification time of the mod folder (or archive file) with the one saved at the last listing. Unchanged: the saved file list is reused. An unreachable folder also keeps its old list rather than becoming empty.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.LIST.desc: A folder mod is walked; an archive is listed from its own index, without extracting it. The new list and date are saved on the mod.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.CACHE.desc: Two in-memory maps: each mod's set of relative paths, and for each path the mods that ship it. Conflicts and the load order read these instead of the disk.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.QUEUE.desc: Mods without hashes are queued at start-up, after a Scan that added mods and after profile changes (when lazy hashing is on). A folder mod whose listing changed and that already had hashes is queued to refresh its baseline.
docs.diagram.mod-sync.n.WORKER.desc: One low-priority thread hashes one mod at a time with BLAKE3, as a Hash operation of the disk governor that yields to deploys and game sessions, and reports each mod's status to the cards.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.title: Modpacks: build, share, apply
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.summary: How a pack records its mods by id and by content hash, travels as a signed .bmp, and is checked, repaired and applied.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.EDITOR.desc: Name, description, target game, the mods in the pack's own order, whether to follow each mod's dependencies, optional download links for repairs, where the pack goes in the activation order, and whether to skip the integrity check.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.MOD_REF.desc: For each mod added, every file is listed with its size and its BLAKE3 hash (tagged b3:), read from the extracted view for an archived mod. That manifest is what lets another PC recognise the same mod.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.PACK_FILE.de: One JSON file per pack in BMM's data folder, with its creation and update dates. The list shows them most recently changed first.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.EXPORT.desc: Writes the pack as a .bmp file, signed with your identity key when the keyring is available (otherwise written unsigned). It holds the list and the hashes, not the mods' files. Importing does not require a signature.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.IMPORT.desc: A .bmp picked from disk, or downloaded from a modpack catalogue (with the catalogue's password and key proof), goes through the same importer and is saved under a new id.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.SWITCH.desc: The switch on a pack card turns the pack on or off in the active profile.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.MATCH.desc: Each pack entry is looked up by its mod id, then by hash in one backend call. An entry found neither way counts as missing. Dependencies are followed one level, only for entries that ask for it.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.ANY_ON: One of its mods already on?
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.ANY_ON.desc: If any mod of the pack found here is on, the switch shows the pack as active and turning it off disables those mods. A pack none of whose mods can be matched is never shown as active.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.CHECK.desc: Unless the pack skips it, every file of the manifest must exist locally with the same size and hash. Each mod comes back valid, missing or corrupted.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.REPAIR.desc: Lists the missing and corrupted mods; Repair downloads them from the entry's link or the pack's server repository, then checks again. With errors and mods still missing it stops; otherwise the pack is applied.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.TOGGLE: Turn the mods on or off
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.TOGGLE.desc: Each found mod is enabled or disabled one at a time, each one on its own: a mod refused (missing hash, archive that cannot be extracted) costs that mod, not the pack.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.ORDER.desc: Once on, the pack's mods are placed in the profile's activation order as one block, by the pack's order mode or the setting: on top (the pack wins), at the bottom, or keep what is already active where it is.
docs.diagram.modpack-flow.n.RESULT.desc: One message: applied, applied with some mods missing, or the names of the mods that could not be toggled (up to three). The Library is refreshed.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.title: mtime cache (mod file lists)
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.summary: How BMM reuses each mod's file list while its folder's modification time is unchanged, and what happens when it changed.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.CALLER.desc: Listing the mods (get_mods), asking for a mod's conflicts, enabling a mod and the load-order tools all need every mod's file list first. They all call ensure_cache_populated.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.FRESH.desc: Once built, the in-memory cache is served as is until something resets it. Only a reset makes the next call look at the folders again.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.INVALIDATE.de: invalidate_cache runs after adding, removing or downloading a mod, a folder scan, a profile change, the mapper and modpack apply. flush_mem_caches empties it to free memory whenever the user leaves the Library, unless mods are being turned on or off.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.MTIME.desc: The modification time of the mod's FOLDER (or archive), in seconds, not of each file. If the metadata cannot be read, the error is logged and the time counts as 0, which never matches.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.SAME.desc: A hit needs a stored file list, a stored last_scan_mtime equal to the current one, and a time that is not 0. Editing a file in place may leave the folder's time unchanged: that is still a hit, because the list itself did not change.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.REUSE.desc: The cached_files saved with the mod are used without walking the folder at all.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.REACHABLE.des: A folder mod whose folder is gone (an unplugged external drive) keeps its old list instead of being emptied, so nothing is re-hashed or rewritten while the drive is away.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.RELIST.desc: A folder mod is walked again. An archived mod is listed from the archive's index, never extracted here, because this runs while the app's state is locked.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.REHASH.desc: A folder mod that already has hashes joins the background SHA queue, after the locks are released. When the worker reaches it, the new hashes replace the old baseline.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.INDEX.desc: In memory only: each mod's set of files, and for each file path the mods that ship it. It is rebuilt whole on every pass, so a deleted mod leaves nothing behind.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.SAVE.desc: The new list and folder time are stored on the mod (cached_files, last_scan_mtime), so the next start can reuse them.
docs.diagram.mtime-cache.n.CONFLICTS.des: Overlapping files between mods are found by looking each file up in the index, without touching the disk.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.title: Offline detection
docs.diagram.offline-mode.summary: How BMM decides it is offline, and what that changes: a banner and an event, never a lock on network features.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.BOOT.desc: The app shell loads the offline module after start-up and runs a first check right away.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.OS.desc: navigator.onLine and the window online and offline events. They only say whether a network interface is up, not whether the internet answers: going offline is believed at once, coming back is checked with a probe.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.TIMERS.desc: A probe every 15 seconds while offline, to notice the return quickly, and every 2 minutes in any case, to catch a connection that died silently.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.PROBE.desc: Runs one at a time. If the system already says there is no network, the answer is offline without any request.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.ENDPOINTS.de: www.gstatic.com/generate_204, then cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace, each with a 5-second timeout, in no-cors mode, nothing cached. Any answer, even an opaque one, counts.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.REACH.desc: The first endpoint that answers ends the probe as online; both failing means offline.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.ONLINE.desc: Normal operation. The banner slides away if it was shown.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.OFFLINE.desc: Nothing is switched off. The state only changes what the next two boxes show.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.BANNER.desc: A small banner at the top of the window, shown while offline and hidden as soon as a probe succeeds.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.EVENT.desc: Fired on the window each time the state changes, with online true or false; window.bmmIsOnline() reads the current state. They are there for any module that wants to react; no module listens today.
docs.diagram.offline-mode.n.NOTLOCK.desc: Repo syncs, catalogues and update checks are not blocked: a repo on your LAN, the built-in repo server and the local API need no internet, and a block keyed on reaching the probe endpoints would stop them too. A feature that really needs the internet fails with its own error; everything local keeps working.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.title: One-click mod install
docs.diagram.one-click-install.summary: How a bmm://install link on a web page becomes a new mod in your library, and what is checked on the way.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.URL.des: A button on a site, in Discord or in a catalog pointing at bmm://install?url=...&name=... (import and download are accepted as the same action). url is the file to fetch, name the suggested mod name.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.OS.desc: BMM registers the bmm:// protocol with Windows at start-up. If BMM is already running, the second launch hands the link to the open window; if not, the link is held until the window is ready, then delivered.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.GATE.de: Every link passes here before anything is fetched. Links can be switched off entirely in the settings. A link from outside the app must give an https address with a host and no credentials in it.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.REFUSED: Links disabled, or an address that is not plain https: nothing is downloaded and a message says why.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.CONFIRM: Shows the mod name (editable), the full address, and a profile list with the active one selected. Nothing happens unless you answer Yes.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.NEW_PRO: Choosing "new profile" asks for a name and the game, mods and backup folders (Yes stays disabled until all four are set), creates it, and installs into it.
Creates a new uniquely named folder in the chosen profile's mods folder and streams the file into it as one Download operation of the disk governor: cancellable, stopped at 4 GiB, never held whole in memory. A cancelled download removes the folder.
Decided from the file's first bytes, not from its name.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.UNZIP.d: Refused up front if the zip declares too much, then capped again while writing. Entries that would escape the folder are skipped. The temporary file is removed whatever happens.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.RAW.des: Anything else (a 7z, a rar, a single file) is kept inside the new folder under its name from the address, not unpacked. A 7z or rar arrives as an archive inside a folder, which the game will not read: use Add a mod for those.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.ENTRY.d: A disabled mod entry is saved with a content_id, exactly like a mod added by hand, and the file index is invalidated.
docs.diagram.one-click-install.n.DONE.de: A toast confirms and the Library refreshes. The mod is not enabled and nothing is written to the game folder until you switch it on.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.title: Performance monitor and benchmark
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.summary: How the live monitor samples BMM's own CPU, memory and disk use, and how the app benchmark times real operations on your disk.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.OPEN.desc: Opened from Settings, a bmm:// link or the local API (which can pre-fill a benchmark and start it). Opening it starts the sampler; closing it stops the sampler unless the mini monitor is open.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.SAMPLER.d: A background loop reads BMM's own process through sysinfo: CPU (per core share), memory, disk read and write, uptime. It emits one benchmark-point event per sample until stop_benchmark. No network probe: the old ping to a third-party site was removed.
Samples every 500 ms instead of every second, refreshes the whole system, and adds virtual memory, swap and whole-machine CPU to each point.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.CHARTS.de: Keeps the last 3600 points and draws them on the next frame: charts, sparklines, an activity map. View the last 1, 5 or 15 minutes or all, drag to zoom, or pause recording and replay a moment.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.MINI.desc: A small always-on-top window of its own, so it stays visible over a game. It listens to the same points and can pause, resume or bring back the full monitor; its capability only allows events and moving or closing itself.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.SESSION_F: A monitored session exports to CSV and imports back for review. Everything stays on this PC.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.RUN.desc: Runs off the UI thread and refuses a second run while one is still in flight; the window retries for a moment when a cancelled run is still aborting.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.DATASET.d: Sandbox builds a synthetic file tree (small, medium, large, very large, or a custom size up to 8 GB and 200,000 files). My mods copies the chosen profiles or folders instead.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.SANDBOX.d: A deterministic tree of generated files in the system temp folder, the same every run, so two runs on two machines compare.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.MY_MODS.d: At most 200 MB and 6000 files copied into a work folder on the SAME drive as the source, so the numbers are that disk's. Falls back to the temp folder if the drive is not writable.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.STEPS.des: Scan, BLAKE3 hashing, copy at full speed and with Smart I/O, zip extraction, activating a mod and an archived mod, deactivating, cancel latency, BLAKE3 verify. Each is repeated and reported as median, min and max with throughput.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.CANCEL.de: Sets a flag checked at every step and between repetitions of the long ones, so the run stops quickly and reports cancelled.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.REPORT.de: Per operation: time, throughput and the spread of samples, with arrows against an earlier run (up to six kept, imported reports included). Exports as JSON, CSV or a standalone HTML page.
docs.diagram.perf-monitoring.n.TELEMETRY: Only with telemetry accepted AND the benchmark option ticked: a quick sandbox run at most once a week, a minute after start, sent as a benchmark event.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.title: Profile colour, icon and background
docs.diagram.profile-customization.summa: How a profile's colour, icon and cropped background are chosen, processed and stored next to data.json.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.LOO: The colour and the icon picked from the built-in grid travel with the other profile fields in create_profile or update_profile. Nothing is processed: they are stored as text.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.PIC: An image file picked from disk replaces the built-in icon. It is only previewed in the dialog; nothing is written before Save.
A PNG, JPG, WEBP or BMP picked in the create or edit dialog opens the cropper. Removing the background is also only recorded until Save.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.CRO: Cropper.js inside the app's modal shell gives the crop box. In the create dialog the box is only kept, because no profile id exists yet; it is applied right after the profile is created.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.SAV: The image changes are applied only when the dialog is saved, after the profile itself: import the icon or remove it, apply the cropped background or remove it.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.IMP: Copies the file as is, without decoding it, as icon_<id>.<ext> and deletes an older icon with another extension. The copy goes through the governor.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.CRO: Decodes the image, refuses a crop box outside it, crops and encodes WebP as temp_bg_<id>.webp. It runs off the main thread, so a 4K image does not freeze the window.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.TIC: All image work holds an Image ticket of the resource governor: it shows in Live activity and can be paused or cancelled between steps. The helpers refuse to run without one.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.APP: Renames temp_bg_<id>.webp to bg_<id>.webp and records it on the profile. It fails if the temporary file is missing.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.REM: Clears the field on the profile, saves, then deletes the image file.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.FIL: bg_<id>.webp and icon_<id>.<ext> sit in BMM's data folder, next to data.json, not in the profile's game or mods folders.
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.DAT: The profile stores color, icon, background_image and icon_image (file names only).
docs.diagram.profile-customization.n.CAR: When the Profiles screen draws, it asks for each profile's background and icon paths and shows them; a missing file simply shows no image.
docs.diagram.profile-system.title: Profiles: create, switch, edit, delete
docs.diagram.profile-system.summary: What a profile is on disk, and what each profile action really changes (switching moves no file).
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.FORM.desc: Asks for a name, the game (destination) folder, the mods folder and an optional backup folder. Each folder is checked as you type: it must exist, the mods folder cannot be the game folder, and a backup folder already used by another profile is refused. A mods folder shared with another profile is allowed after a warning.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.CREATE.des: Refuses a game or mods folder that does not exist, gives the profile a new unique id and an empty list of active mods, and saves. The dialog then makes the new profile the active one.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.BACKUP_GIV: The backup folder is the only one BMM can choose for you. The game and mods folders stay required.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.BACKUP_AUT: Left blank, the backup folder is created under BMM's own data folder, named after the profile id, so two profiles can never share it even with the same name. It holds the game files that mods replaced.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.EDIT.desc: Saves the new name, folders, colour and icon. The game and mods folders must still exist.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.REHASH.des: When the mods folder moves, the in-memory file cache is dropped and the mods without hashes are queued for the throttled background hashing.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.DATA.desc: Every profile lives here: id, name, game_path, mods_path, backup_path, active_mods (in activation order), colour and images, plus active_profile_id. Saved crash-safe with a rolling data.json.bak.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.SHARE.desc: Several profiles may point at the same game folder. BMM then treats the files their mods deployed there as mods' files, never as game originals, and a mod cannot be enabled twice in that folder.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.CARDS.desc: One card per profile with its folders, disk usage, active mods, colour, icon and background. The active profile is highlighted.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.SWITCH.des: Only changes active_profile_id and saves. No file is copied or removed: each profile's enabled mods stay deployed in its own game folder. The Library and the Discord status are refreshed.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.LIBRARY.de: The Library lists the active profile's mods, and every toggle, order list or modpack applies to that profile. Files move only there.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.BULK_OFF.d: disable_mods_for_profiles turns off every mod of the selected profiles (or all profiles), or chosen mods wherever they are active, grouped by game and backup folder.
docs.diagram.profile-system.n.DELETE.des: Removes the profile entry only; another profile becomes active if needed. It does not disable its mods nor touch the game, mods or backup folders.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.title: Downloading only what is missing
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.summary: How a repo sync reuses what is already on disk, fetches only the 4 MB chunks that changed, caps and paces every transfer, and checks the result.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.g.DECID: For each file in the manifest
The manifest lists each file with its size, its SHA-256 and the SHA-256 of each 4 MB chunk. Those chunk hashes are what makes a partial fetch possible.
The local copy is hashed and compared with the manifest. Equal: nothing is transferred. "Overwrite all" and a file listed with no hash always go on to the download.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.n.CHUNK: A patch is possible when the old file exists, the manifest lists its chunks and the source is HTTP. Over SFTP the whole file is read.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.n.RANGE: Each local 4 MB chunk is hashed; for every one that differs, a Range request fetches just those bytes and writes them in place, then the file is cut to its listed size. A small change to a large file costs a few MB. It needs a server that honours Range, as static web servers do; BMM's own servers send the whole file instead.
Streamed to disk chunk by chunk, never held in memory. A mod published as a single zip is streamed to a staging file, then extracted or kept as an archived mod. An SSH source reads the file over the sync's one SFTP session.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.n.CAP.d: Every download stops at 4 GiB: the announced Content-Length is checked first, then the bytes actually received. Writes follow the disk governor's Download rate for the target disk, and the sync's own download limit (KB/s) when one is set.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.n.PAUSE: Checked between files and between mods, from the sync's buttons or the resources dashboard. Pause waits without losing anything; Cancel stops and removes the profile folders this sync created.
docs.diagram.resumable-downloads.n.VERIF: The finished file, patched or not, is hashed again and compared with the manifest. A file listed with no hash is kept and its mod is marked unverified.
Counted in the sync summary (files and bytes downloaded); a skipped file costs nothing but its hash.
A hash mismatch (repo.errIntegrity) or the size cap (download.tooLarge) ends the sync with that error; a whole-file download cut by the cap is deleted. There is no automatic retry.
The Laya offline pack is the one download that resumes where it stopped: it hashes what laya-offline.zip.part already holds and asks for the rest with Range. A server that ignores the range makes it start over. The finished pack must match its pinned size and SHA-256.
docs.diagram.scheduler.summary: How a task is stored, when the engine decides it is due, how its steps run, and which steps need a permission.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.EDITOR.desc: Builds a task as blocks, as a flow chart or as BMMScript code, all three on the same step tree, from scratch or from a preset. A task imported from a .bmmpa file arrives disabled, with every permission reset to off.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.TASKS.desc: The whole task list, saved as one JSON array in BMM's app data folder. The front end owns its shape; Rust only checks that it is an array.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.TICK.desc: While BMM is open, each enabled task's trigger is checked: a clock (once, every N minutes or hours, daily, weekly, monthly, with catch-up of a missed window), BMM start, a watched file, a BMM event, another task finishing, a script that exits 0, a condition becoming true, or a new RSS or Atom item. The first tick is 4 seconds after launch.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.OS_TASK.desc: Optional, for clock triggers and the start trigger (which becomes at Windows logon): BMM registers a Windows task named BMM_<id> that opens a bmm://schedule/run link with a key kept on this machine, so the task runs even when BMM was closed.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.MANUAL.desc: The Run button, or a bmm://schedule/run?id= link. A link asks for confirmation first, naming the task, unless it carries this machine's key from the Windows task.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.GAME_HOLD.desc: When game mode is on and its Hold scheduled tasks option is ticked, a due task is not run but kept as owed, and runs on the first tick after the game ends.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.RUN.desc: Opens a run context with the task's variables, a snapshot of the shared variables and what the triggering event carried as {event.*}. It shows in the running panel with a Stop button, and a failed run can be retried from the start up to 5 times.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.STEPS.desc: Actions, delays, wait-until, if/else, switch, loops (repeat, for each), try, retry, ensure, parallel branches, calls to saved blocks, break, continue and stop. Conditions read BMM's state and the run's variables; Stop is honoured between steps.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.ACTION.desc: More than a hundred action types (profiles, mods, modpacks, repos, apps, themes, storage, variables, files, notifications...) dispatched to the same commands the buttons use. An action can write variables that later steps and conditions read.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.PERMS.desc: Running programs, scripts, bmm:// links, stopping processes, changing resources, deleting, running other tasks, network access and asking Laya each need their own grant on the task. Only the value true counts as a grant.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.EXEC.desc: Run in Rust: a command never goes through a shell string, a script runs through its engine (PowerShell, CMD, Bash, Python, Node, Rust). Webhooks, Discord, Slack and feeds are http(s) only, refuse private addresses unless the step allows the local network, and have a timeout and a size cap.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.LAYA.desc: ai.classify, ai.ask and ai.suggest_mod_metadata. At most 20 calls and 120 seconds per run, plus 30 calls per minute across all tasks. Free text from the model is marked untrusted and can only go into messages, logs and file contents; a classification can only answer one of the task's own labels.
docs.diagram.scheduler.n.RESULT.desc: Ok, stopped on purpose, cancelled or failed: a toast, the last 20 runs in the task, a detailed run log in TaskRuns/<id>.jsonl (50 runs or 2 MB per task, secrets removed), and a bmm.task.done event that other tasks can trigger on.
docs.diagram.security-system.title: Security model: what BMM checks
docs.diagram.security-system.summary: How far the interface can read your disks, and the checks Rust applies to everything that comes from outside: links, the local API, custom pages, repositories and updates.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.UI.desc: Asked once at first launch (it must be answered) and changeable in Settings, or preset by the installer. Applied at every start and again right after a change.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.MODE.desc: fs_security_mode decides which folders the interface may read through Tauri's file scope and the asset:// protocol (mod images, previews). BMM's own folders are always allowed. Rust commands are not limited by this scope: they apply their own checks.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.FULL.desc: Every mounted disk is added to the scope, so the interface can show files from anywhere.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.LIMITED.d: Only the game, mods and backup folders of each profile are added, at start and whenever a profile is created or edited.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.PATHS.des: A path that comes from a manifest, a link or an id must be relative: no root, no drive letter or colon, no .. segment (also with trailing dots or spaces). An id that becomes a folder name must be a single component.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.OUTSIDE.d: A web page firing a bmm:// link, another program on this PC, a shared navbar file, a repository server, the release host.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.LINKS.des: BMM asks before a link changes anything. Even then, a link may only launch a registered app by id, install over https with a matching SHA-256, never run a script, and never reach a network share.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.API.desc: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only and accepts only a 127.0.0.1 or localhost Host header, against DNS rebinding. Protected routes need the API token, compared in constant time; an empty token never matches.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.PAGES.des: Sandboxed frames that reach BMM only through the broker. Every page command re-checks the page id and its granted permissions in Rust, and an imported page starts with none.
Checked before sync writes anything. A manifest that carries a signature or an author id must verify (ed25519). A repo listed in the official list must serve exactly the signature recorded there: missing or different is refused. A manifest with no signature at all syncs as unsigned.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.REPO_HASH: Each downloaded file must match the SHA-256 in the manifest, or the sync stops. A file listed with no hash is kept, and its mod is marked unverified.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.UPDATE.de: Verified with the publisher key built into BMM: right app id, valid for at most 7 days and not expired, a strictly newer version, every file over https with a SHA-256 and a plain relative path.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.INSTALLER: A full installer is run only if the signed manifest lists that exact URL with its SHA-256, the download (1 GB cap) matches it, and it is saved under a name from the manifest in a new temporary folder.
docs.diagram.security-system.n.REFUSED.d: The operation stops before writing or running anything, with the reason shown. There is no trust anyway option for a bad signature or a hash mismatch.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.title: Search and semantic mode
docs.diagram.semantic-search.summary: What the three search boxes do with your words: synonym expansion, the ranking, and the offline Ask Laya index.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.PALETTE.d: The command palette searches commands, mods, profiles, themes, plugins, settings, docs pages and the current page at once. A Classic / Semantic switch decides whether the query is widened with synonyms.
The box at the top of the docs hub, with its own Classic / Semantic switch. It looks through the hub's articles, the diagrams and the bundled documentation pages, in both languages.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.LIB_BOX.d: Off by default: the library box filters by name and tag. On, the query also goes to the Ask index restricted to mods, and the list follows the order it returns. A question typed there (a question mark, or four words) plus Enter opens Ask Laya.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.MODE.desc: Classic keeps the words you typed. Semantic adds, for each word, every word of the synonym group it belongs to. There is no embedding or vector model behind this mode.
Each language file can carry a _synonyms block. The groups of every loaded language are merged, so a French word can bring in its English equivalents and the other way round.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.PROVIDERS: Every source registers a provider; all are asked in parallel and the run is cut after 1.5 s, so one slow source cannot freeze the palette. Only the commands provider receives the synonyms, as hidden keywords: mods, docs and the rest are matched on the words typed.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.SCORER.de: Accents are folded, then each word scores exact, prefix, word start, substring or scattered letters, weighted by field (title above subtitle above keywords). Every word must match somewhere; ties break on title length.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.COUNT.des: The docs hub ranks by how many of the (expanded) terms appear in a result's text. Up to 12 bundled pages are listed, and a page that already backs an article is not listed twice.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.ASK_UI.de: Opened from the palette's Ask row (a typed question), the docs hub button or the library box. The question is sent to Rust with the app's Settings cards as extra index entries.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.BM25.desc: A BM25 index over the bundled docs sections, hub articles and commands (ask_index.gen.json), the Settings cards, and the user's mods and profiles. The intent is routed by keyword rules; file and conflict questions are answered exactly from the mods' file lists.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.RERANK.de: Only when AI is on, Ask is allowed and the embedded model is installed: one choice question over the top 6 candidates plus "none of these", averaged with the retrieval score. Nothing leaves the PC.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.n.RESULTS.d: A list of things that exist, each with its action: open a page, run a command, go to a setting, show a mod or its files. No text is written by a model on this path.
docs.diagram.semantic-search.e.question: a question
docs.diagram.server-mode.title: Subscribing to a repo and syncing it
docs.diagram.server-mode.summary: What the repo server checks on every request, and how a sync refuses a bad manifest before writing, fetches only what changed and verifies every file.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.FETCH.desc: Reads repo.json from the link ("/repo.json" is added when missing). When the manifest carries a seed, it is fetched again with a creator id salted with that seed, so each repo sees a different id. The download password goes as X-Repo-Password, plus a key proof when a key is set for that origin.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.SIGCARD.desc: The card shows one of five states before anything is downloaded: valid, unsigned, invalid, missing or mismatch. The last three disable Sync with the reason. missing and mismatch only apply to a repo pinned in the official repo list, whose recorded signature must be served unchanged.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.GATE.desc: Runs on every file, repo.json included, in this order: the download password (header or ?password=), the key proof when public keys are listed, a creator id (required for anything under mods/), the BetterCommunity attestation when the repo requires a login, then the ban list and the whitelist. The built-in server also refuses its own server files and any path with "..".
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.DENIED.desc: A 401 makes BMM ask for the download password and retry. A 403 is reported as banned, not on the whitelist (with a hint to link an account) or forbidden. Nothing is installed.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.MANIFEST.desc: The profiles, their mods and every file with its size, SHA-256 and 4 MB chunk hashes, signed with the author's ed25519 key. A server with no repo.json is read from its folder listing instead: those files have no hash and the mods install as unverified.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.SIGGATE.desc: Checked before anything is written. A manifest that carries a signature or an author id must verify; a pinned repo must serve exactly its recorded signature. Any file path that could land outside its mod folder (absolute, "..", a drive or ":") refuses the whole manifest.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.REFUSED.desc: The sync stops with repo.errSignatureInvalid, repo.errSignatureMissing, repo.errSignatureMismatch or repo.errUnsafePath. There is no override.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.SAME.desc: For each file of each selected mod, the local copy is hashed. Equal to the manifest: skipped. "Overwrite all" and a manifest with no hash always re-fetch.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.DOWNLOAD.desc: Over HTTP, only the 4 MB chunks that differ are fetched with Range when the old file is there; otherwise the whole file is streamed. An SSH source reads the file over one SFTP session. A mod published as a single zip is downloaded, then extracted or kept as an archived mod.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.VERIFY.desc: Every downloaded file is hashed again and compared with the manifest. A file listed with no hash is kept, and its mod is marked unverified.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.STOPPED.desc: A hash mismatch stops the sync with repo.errIntegrity. Cancel stops it at the next file and removes the profile folders this sync created.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.CLEAN.desc: Files in a mod folder that the manifest no longer lists are deleted. With "delete extra", whole mod folders (named id_name) that the repo no longer has are removed too.
docs.diagram.server-mode.n.SAVED.desc: The profile is created or updated, each mod records the repo it came from (and the author's update sources) so the update checker can follow it, and the first synced profile becomes the active one. The summary reports added, updated and removed mods and the signature state.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.title: Telemetry pipeline
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.summary: Opt-in telemetry from the consent dialog to the server: the five categories, the local queue, the sending, and the erase and export controls.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.CONSEN: Shown once, after the terms and privacy dialogs, while no answer is stored. The answer is saved in data.json; it can be changed in Settings, and a bmm:// link can only ask, never switch it on by itself.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.NOTHIN: No answer or a refusal: no event is tracked or queued, Rust refuses every track and flush. Turning telemetry off stops collection and deletes the local queue and the live errors queue.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.CATEGO: Five switches under the one consent: usage, performance, Laya statistics, errors, session replay. An event whose category is off is dropped before it reaches Rust; the anonymous hardware profile goes with any of them.
Views entered and left, clicks on known controls, opened dialogs, a frame-rate sample every 30 s and web vitals, plus warning and error lines of the console and of the Rust log. Hidden or idle windows send nothing.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.LAYA_S: Each finished ai_ command becomes a content-free event: feature, provider, duration, whether it answered, which fields were suggested and kept. Never a question, a mod or file name, or an error message.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.REPLAY: An rrweb recording of the window, started when the app is idle. Typed values and mod, profile and path names are masked by default; an unmasked recording is a manual choice in Settings, never from a link.
Checks the consent again (hard gate), then the sampling the server sent (an install is fully in or out of each kind), and appends one line to the queue. Nothing is added once the queue passes 10 MB.
One JSON event per line in the app data folder. It survives restarts and offline periods, and Settings can export it as it stands.
Every 90 s while the window is visible, and before it closes. The end of a session also goes out as a single beacon so it is not lost when the window closes.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.ENDPOI: The endpoint comes from links.json (the BetterCommunity telemetry service by default). Only https, or plain http to this PC for development, is accepted; empty or anything else keeps the events in the queue.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.SEND.d: Sends the whole queue as one gzipped packet with a random packet id. The queue is cleared only after a success; a network error keeps it. The packet's id, time and event counts are logged in analytics_sent.json (last 500).
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.SERVER: Stores the packets and answers each one with the current sampling document, kept in telemetry_sampling.json for the next events. It also reports each sent packet's status.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.GDPR.d: In Settings: export or clear the local queue, ask the server to erase any sent packet (applied after a review delay of up to 72 h), or request a copy of your data by e-mail.
docs.diagram.telemetry-pipeline.n.LIVE_E: The errors category: panics, window errors and failed operations, redacted, grouped by fingerprint, capped per hour and queued on disk, then sent to the service's /issues by their own transport.
docs.diagram.theme-system.title: Theme system
docs.diagram.theme-system.summary: Where a theme comes from, how the editor builds one, and how applying it repaints the whole app from CSS tokens.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.BUILTIN.desc: One JSON file per preset in the bundled builtin-themes folder, sorted by their NN- prefix, followed by drop-in presets from the theme-presets folder in app data (a drop-in reusing a built-in id is ignored). Built-ins cannot be deleted, only hidden and restored.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.INSTALLED.de: Every saved, imported or catalogue theme lives in app data as themes/<id>/theme.json, with its assets and fonts beside it. A theme id that could escape that folder is refused.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.CATALOG.desc: Gallery of the official BMM_Themes catalogue plus community sources (HTTP fetched by the Rust side with the site identity header, ssh:// sources read by the interface, local files), merged and deduplicated by id. Filters by source and by dark or light; Apply, Install, Uninstall and Reinstall act from the preview pane.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.FILE.desc: A .bmmtheme is a ZIP of theme.json with its assets/ and fonts/; import keeps only those entries. Share copies a bmm://theme/import-inline link carrying the theme, which BMM asks to confirm before importing; a theme too large for a link is exported as a file instead.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.EDITOR.desc: A floating, dockable panel with four tabs: Simple (token colours, fonts, sizes, presets), Elements (your own HTML and CSS blocks), Advanced (CSS per page) and Installed. Saving over a built-in always creates a copy under a new name.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.GEN.desc: Builds a complete dark or light set of tokens from a single accent colour, tinting the backgrounds with its hue.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.PICK.desc: Right-click (or middle-click) any element of the app to edit its colours, hover state and CSS. The result is stored as an element override keyed by a CSS selector.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.BOOT.desc: Loads the built-ins, then applies the remembered theme at once, from the built-ins or a cached copy, so there is no flash of the default look. It then reads the installed themes from disk and re-applies the authoritative copy; an id that no longer exists resets to the default.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.APPLY.desc: Writes four <style> blocks: the token values (with r/g/b channels derived for tints), the global and per-page CSS with element overrides, the fonts, and the inline-colour patches. Then it places custom elements, HTML swaps and images (mascot, logo, wallpaper). It never changes a source file.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.TOKENS.desc: css/tokens.css defines the --bmm-* variables on :root, the official theming surface: every other stylesheet reads them. A build gate fails if another stylesheet redefines one, which would pin it in every theme. An animation speed of 0 turns animations off.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.PATCH.desc: A MutationObserver watches content rendered by code and rewrites hardcoded inline colours to the theme's tokens as elements appear, so dynamic screens follow the theme too.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.LIGHT.desc: A theme is light when it says so, or, with no mode set, when its base background is bright. The contrast enforcer is on by default and can be turned off in the editor.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.CONTRAST.des: Finds text too light for the light background behind it and gives it the theme's text token. Each original value is kept and put back when the enforcer is turned off or a dark theme is applied. Editor previews run it 300 ms after the last change.
docs.diagram.theme-system.n.LIVE.desc: Every view follows at once, without reloading. Parts that bake colours in when they render (diagrams, code highlighting, the docs hub) listen for the bmm:theme-applied event and redraw.
docs.diagram.update-system.title: Mod updates
docs.diagram.update-system.summary: How BMM finds newer versions of your mods, from a Server Repo or a direct download link, and applies them only when you choose.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.LINKS.desc: Saved on the mod in data.json: its source repo and repo_mod_id (recorded automatically by a sync), an update URL, extra repos or direct download links set in Configure updates, plus the global update repos from Settings, matched by repo_mod_id.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.REPO.desc: Each repo is fetched once per check, with this installation's creator id. Its manifest lists every mod with its version and changelog.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.DIRECT.desc: A plain URL with no version. BMM reads its ETag, Last-Modified and size with a HEAD request; when the host gives no ETag or date, it hashes the first 64 KB of the file instead. Redirects are followed.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.TRIGGER.des: The buttons on the Repo page and in the library, a single mod's check, or a silent check every N minutes when an interval is set (off by default), first run 8 seconds after launch.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.CHECK.desc: Builds, per mod, the list of repos and links to ask, without duplicates. A mod already found to have an update is not asked again from another source. Returns the updates, the sources that failed, and how many mods were checkable.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.VERSION.des: The repo's version for this repo_mod_id is compared with the installed one. Any difference counts, not only a higher number, so a rollback on the repo shows up too.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.BASELINE.de: The validator is compared with the baseline saved when the link was configured. A changed size, ETag or date is reported as a possible update with what changed; a link seen for the first time only records its baseline.
docs.diagram.update-system.n.NOTHING: Up to date or now tracking
docs.diagram.update-system.n.NOTHING.des: Says everything is up to date, that a first baseline was recorded (re-check later), or that no mod is linked to any source yet, rather than pretending all is current.
